232	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_BUSY,
233	
234	    /* The request was stalled */
235	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_REQUEST_STALLED,
236	
237	    /* A required parameter was invalid */
238	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_INVALID_PARAMETER,
239	
240	    /* The associated device does not exist in the system. */
241	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_DEVICE_UNKNOWN,
242	
243	    /* The transfer or requested was aborted */
244	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_ABORTED,
245	
246	    /* The specified handle is not valid */
247	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_HANDLE_INVALID,
248	
249	    /* The operation was successful */
250	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS /*DOM-IGNORE-BEGIN*/ = 1 /*DOM-IGNORE-END*/
251	
252	} USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT;
253	
254	// *****************************************************************************
255	/*  USB Host CDC Client Driver Command Event Data.
256	 
257	  Summary:
258	     USB Host CDC Client Driver Command Event Data.
259	
260	  Description:
261	    This data type defines the data structure returned by the driver along with
262	    the following events:
263	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE_DATA,
264	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SEND_BREAK_COMPLETE_DATA,
265	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_GET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE_DATA,
266	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE_DATA,
267	
268	  Remarks:
269	    None.
270	*/
271	
272	typedef struct
273	{
274	    /* Request handle of this request */
275	    USB_HOST_CDC_REQUEST_HANDLE requestHandle;
276	
277	    /* Termination status */
278	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT result;
279	
280	    /* Size of the data transferred in the request */
281	    size_t length;
282	}
283	USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_GET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE_DATA,
284	USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE_DATA,
285	USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE_DATA,
286	USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SEND_BREAK_COMPLETE_DATA;
287	
288	// *****************************************************************************
289	/* USB Host CDC Client Driver Event Data.
290	 
291	  Summary:
292	     USB Host CDC Client Driver Event Data.
293	
294	  Description:
295	    This data type defines the data structure returned by the driver along with
296	    the following events:
297	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE_DATA,
298	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE_DATA,
299	
300	  Remarks:
301	    None.
302	*/
303	
304	typedef struct
305	{
306	    /* Transfer handle of this transfer */
307	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE transferHandle;
308	
309	    /* Termination transfer status */
310	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT result;
311	
312	    /* Size of the data transferred in the request */
313	    size_t length;
314	}
315	USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_SERIAL_STATE_NOTIFICATION_RECEIVED_DATA,
316	USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE_DATA,
317	USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE_DATA;
318	
319	// *****************************************************************************
320	/* CDC Class Driver Events
321	
322	  Summary:
323	    Identifies the possible events that the CDC Class Driver can generate.
324	
325	  Description:
326	    This enumeration identifies the possible events that the CDC Class Driver
327	    can generate. The application should register an event handler using the
328	    USB_HOST_CDC_EventHandlerSet function to receive CDC Class Driver events.
329	    
330	    An event may have data associated with it.  Events that are generated due to
331	    a transfer of data between the host and device are accompanied by data
332	    structures that provide the status of the transfer termination. For example,
333	    the USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE event is accompanied by a
334	    pointer to a USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE_DATA data
335	    structure. The transferStatus member of this data structure indicates the
336	    success or failure of the transfer. A transfer may fail due to device not
337	    responding on the bus, if the device stalls any stages of the transfer or
338	    due to NAK timeouts. The event description provides details on the nature of
339	    the event and the data that is associated with the event.
340	
341	  Remarks:
342	    None.
343	*/
344	
345	typedef enum
346	{
347	    /* This event occurs when a CDC Client Driver Read operation has completed
348	       i.e when the data has been received from the connected CDC device. This
349	       event is generated after the application calls the USB_HOST_CDC_Read
350	       function. The eventData parameter in the event call back function will be
351	       of a pointer to a USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE_DATA structure. This
352	       contains details about the transfer handle associated with this read
353	       request, the amount of data read and the termination status of the read
354	       request. */
355	
356	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE,
357	
358	    /* This event occurs when a CDC Client Driver Write operation has completed
359	       i.e when the data has been written to the connected CDC device. This
360	       event is generated after the application calls the USB_HOST_CDC_Write
361	       function. The eventData parameter in the event call back function will be
362	       a pointer to a USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE_DATA structure. This
363	       contains details about the transfer handle associated with this write
364	       request, the amount of data written and the termination status of the write
365	       request. */
366	
367	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE,
368	
369	    /* This event occurs when a CDC Client Driver Send Break 
370	       request has completed. This event is generated after the application
371	       calls the USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_BreakSend function and the device has either
372	       acknowledged or stalled the request. The eventData parameter in the event
373	       call back function will be of a pointer to a
374	       USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE_DATA structure. This
375	       contains details about the transfer handle associated with this request,
376	       the amount of data sent and the termination status of the set request. */
377	
378	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SEND_BREAK_COMPLETE,
379	
380	    /* This event occurs when a CDC Client Driver Set Control Line State 
381	       request has completed. This event is generated after the application
382	       calls the USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_ControlLineStateSet function and the device has
383	       either acknowledged or stalled the request. The eventData parameter in
384	       the event call back function will be of a pointer to a
385	       USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE_DATA structure. This
386	       contains details about the transfer handle associated with this request,
387	       the amount of data sent and the termination status of the set request. */
388	
389	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE,
390	
391	    /* This event occurs when a CDC Client Driver Set Line Coding
392	       request has completed. This event is generated after the application
393	       calls the USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_LineCodingSet function and the device either
394	       acknowledged or stalled the request. The eventData parameter in the event
395	       call back function will be of a pointer to a
396	       USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE_DATA structure. This contains
397	       details about the transfer handle associated with this request, the
398	       amount of data sent and the termination status of the set request. */
399	
400	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE,
401	
402	    /* This event occurs when a CDC Client Driver Get Line Coding
403	       request has completed.  This event is generated after the application
404	       calls the USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_LineCodingGet function and the device sends the
405	       line coding to the host. The eventData parameter in the event call back
406	       function will be of a pointer to a
407	       USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_GET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE_DATA structure.  This
408	       contains details about the transfer handle associated with this request,
409	       the amount of data received and the termination status of the get
410	       request. */
411	
412	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_GET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE,
413	
414	    /* This event occurs when a CDC Client Driver Serial State Notification
415	       Get operation has completed.  This event is generated after the
416	       application calls the USB_HOST_CDC_SerialStateNotificationGet and the
417	       device sends a serial state notification to the host. The eventData
418	       parameter in the event call back function will be of a pointer to a
419	       USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_SERIAL_STATE_NOTIFICATION_RECEIVED_DATA structure.
420	       This contains details about the transfer handle associated with this
421	       request, the amount of data received and the termination status of the
422	       get request. */
423	
424	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_SERIAL_STATE_NOTIFICATION_RECEIVED,
425	
426	    /* This event occurs when the device that this client was connected to has
427	     * been detached. The client should close the CDC instance. There is no
428	     * event data associated with this event */
429	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_DEVICE_DETACHED
430	
431	} USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT;
432	
433	// *****************************************************************************
434	/* USB Host CDC Client Driver Attach Event Handler Function Pointer Type.
435	
436	  Summary:
437	    USB Host CDC Client Driver Attach Event Handler Function Pointer Type.
438	
439	  Description:
440	    This data type defines the required function signature of the USB Host CDC
441	    Client Driver attach event handling callback function. The application must
442	    register a pointer to a CDC Client Driver attach events handling function
443	    whose function signature (parameter and return value types) match the types
444	    specified by this function pointer in order to receive attach event call
445	    backs from the CDC Client Driver. The client driver will invoke this
446	    function with event relevant parameters. The description of the event
447	    handler function parameters is given here.
448	
449	    cdcObjHandle - Handle of the client to which this event is directed.
450	    
451	    context - Value identifying the context of the application that was
452	    registered along with  the event handling function.
453	
454	  Remarks:
455	    None.
456	*/
457	
458	typedef void (* USB_HOST_CDC_ATTACH_EVENT_HANDLER)
459	(
460	    USB_HOST_CDC_OBJ cdcObjHandle, 
461	    uintptr_t context
462	);
463	
464	// *****************************************************************************
465	/* USB Host CDC Event Handler Return Type 
466	 
467	  Summary: 
468	    Return type of the USB CDC Host Client Driver Event Handler.
469	
470	  Description:
471	    This enumeration list the possible return values of the USB CDC Host Client
472	    Driver Event Handler.
473	
474	  Remarks:
475	    None.
476	*/
477	
478	typedef enum
479	{
480	    /* This means no response is required */
481	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_RESPONE_NONE   /*DOM-IGNORE-BEGIN*/= 0 /*DOM-IGNORE-END*/
482	
483	} USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE;
484	
485	// *****************************************************************************
486	/* USB Host CDC Client Driver Event Handler Function Pointer Type.
487	
488	  Summary:
489	    USB Host CDC Client Driver Event Handler Function Pointer Type.
490	
491	  Description:
492	    This data type defines the required function signature of the USB Host CDC
493	    Client Driver event handling callback function. The application must
494	    register a pointer to a CDC Client Driver events handling function whose
495	    function signature (parameter and return value types) match the types
496	    specified by this function pointer in order to receive event call backs from
497	    the CDC Client Driver. The class driver will invoke this function with
498	    event relevant parameters. The description of the event handler function
499	    parameters is given here.
500	
501	    handle - Handle of the client to which this event is directed.
502	    
503	    event - Type of event generated.
504	    
505	    eventData - This parameter should be type casted to a event specific pointer
506	    type based on the event that has occurred. Refer to the USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT
507	    enumeration description for more details.
508	    
509	    context - Value identifying the context of the application that was
510	    registered along with  the event handling function.
511	
512	  Remarks:
513	    None.
514	*/
515	
516	typedef USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE (* USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_HANDLER)
517	(
518	    USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE cdcHandle,
519	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT event,
520	    void * eventData,
521	    uintptr_t context
522	);

752	// ****************************************************************************
753	/* Function:
754	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT USB_HOST_CDC_Write
755	    (
756	        USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
757	        USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE * transferHandle,
758	        void * data,
759	        size_t size
760	    );
761	           
762	  Summary:
763	    This function will write data to the attached device.
764	
765	  Description:
766	    This function will write data to the attached CDC device. The function will
767	    write size amount of bytes. If the request was accepted, transferHandle will
768	    contain a valid transfer handle, else it will contain
769	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID. The completion of the request will be
770	    indicated by the USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE event. The transfer
771	    handle will be returned in the event. 
772	
773	  Precondition:
774	    The client handle should be valid.
775	
776	  Input:
777	    handle - handle to the CDC device instance to which the request should be
778	    sent.
779	    
780	    transferHandle - Pointer to USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE type of a variable.
781	    This will contain a valid transfer handle if the request was successful.
782	
783	    data - pointer to the buffer containing the data to be written. The
784	    contents of the buffer should not be changed till the
785	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE event has occurred.
786	
787	    size - Number of bytes to write.
788	
789	  Return:
790	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS - The operation was successful.
791	
792	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_DEVICE_UNKNOWN - The device that this request was
793	    targeted to does not exist in the system.
794	
795	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_BUSY - The request could not be scheduled at this time.
796	    The client should try again.
797	
798	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_INVALID_PARAMETER - An input parameter was NULL.
799	
800	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_FAILURE - An unknown failure occurred.
801	
802	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_HANDLE_INVALID - The client handle is not valid.
803	    
804	  Example:
805	    <code>
806	    </code>
807	
808	  Remarks:
809	    None.                                                                   
810	*/
811	
812	USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT USB_HOST_CDC_Write
813	(
814	    USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
815	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE * transferHandle,
816	    void * data,
817	    size_t size
818	);

821	/* Function:
822	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT USB_HOST_CDC_Read
823	    (
824	        USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
825	        USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE * transferHandle,
826	        void * data,
827	        size_t size
828	    );
829	           
830	  Summary:
831	    This function will read data from the attached device.
832	
833	  Description:
834	    This function will read data from the attached CDC device. The function will
835	    try to read size amount of bytes but will stop reading when the device
836	    terminates the USB transfer (sends a short packet or a ZLP). If the request
837	    was accepted, transferHandle will contain a valid transfer handle, else it
838	    will contain USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID. The completion of the
839	    request will be indicated by the USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE
840	    event. The transfer handle will be returned in the event. 
841	
842	  Precondition:
843	    The client handle should be valid.
844	
845	  Input:
846	    handle - handle to the CDC device instance to which the request should be
847	    sent.
848	    
849	    transferHandle - Pointer to USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE type of a variable.
850	    This will contain a valid transfer handle if the request was successful.
851	
852	    data - pointer to the buffer where the received data will be stored. The
853	    contents of the buffer will be valid only when the
854	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE event has occurred.
855	
856	    size - size of the data buffer. Only these many bytes or less will be read.
857	
858	  Return:
859	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS - The operation was successful.
860	
861	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_DEVICE_UNKNOWN - The device that this request was
862	    targeted to does not exist in the system.
863	
864	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_BUSY - The request could not be scheduled at this time.
865	    The client should try again.
866	
867	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_INVALID_PARAMETER - An input parameter was NULL.
868	
869	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_FAILURE - An unknown failure occurred.
870	
871	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_HANDLE_INVALID - The client handle is not valid.
872	    
873	  Example:
874	    <code>
875	    </code>
876	
877	  Remarks:
878	    None.                                                                   
879	*/
880	
881	USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT USB_HOST_CDC_Read
882	(
883	    USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
884	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE * transferHandle,
885	    void * data,
886	    size_t size
887	);

889	// ****************************************************************************
890	/* Function:
891	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT USB_HOST_CDC_SerialStateNotificationGet
892	    (
893	        USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
894	        USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE * transferHandle,
895	        USB_CDC_SERIAL_STATE * serialState
896	    );
897	           
898	  Summary:
899	    This function will request Serial State Notification from the attached
900	    device.
901	
902	  Description:
903	    This function will request Serial State Notification from the attached
904	    device. If the request was accepted, transferHandle will contain a valid
905	    transfer handle, else it will contain USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID.
906	    The completion of the request will be indicated by the
907	    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_SERIAL_STATE_NOTIFICATION_RECEIVED event. The transfer
908	    handle will be returned in the event. 
909	
910	  Precondition:
911	    The client handle should be valid.
912	
913	  Input:
914	    handle - handle to the CDC device instance to which the request should be
915	    sent.
916	    
917	    transferHandle - Pointer to USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE type of a variable.
918	    This will contain a valid transfer handle if the request was successful.
919	
920	    serialState - Pointer to the serial state data structure where the received

219	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
220	{
221	    (void)param;
222	
223	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started\r\n");
224	
225	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
226	
227	    for (;;)
228	    {
229	        if (s_cdc_obj_valid && s_cdc_handle == USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID)
230	        {
231	            s_cdc_obj_valid = false;
232	            (void)open_cdc(s_cdc_obj_pending);
233	        }
234	
235	        uint8_t mask;
236	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
237	        {
238	            last_mask = mask;
239	        }
240	        else
241	        {
242	            mask = last_mask;
243	        }
244	
245	        if (s_connected)
246	        {
247	            (void)send_one_byte(mask);
248	        }
249	    }
250	}

252	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
253	{
254	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
255	                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
256	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
257	                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
258	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
259	
260	    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
261	    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);
262	
263	    s_ctrl_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_ctrl_done_buf);
264	    configASSERT(s_ctrl_done != NULL);
265	
266	    /* Register the CDC attach listener before the bus is enabled — the host
267	     * stack only matches a class driver if its attach handler is in place
268	     * when enumeration completes. App-level USB_HOST_BusEnable runs right
269	     * after this init returns. */
270	    (void)USB_HOST_CDC_AttachEventHandlerSet(cdc_attach_handler, 0u);
271	
272	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
273	                                       "FretLink",

275	                                       NULL,
276	                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
277	                                       s_task_stack,
278	                                       &s_task_tcb);
279	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);
280	}

287	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
288	{
289	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
290	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
291	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
292	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled USB write from accumulating
293	     * stale chord state. */
294	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
295	
296	    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
297	    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
298	    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }
299	
300	    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
301	                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
302	}

**1. frame_epoch source & increment site:**
`frame_epoch` is `ISC_Capture.g_frame_count` directly. Increment happens in **firmware/marvin/default/src/video/isc_capture.c:62** (`g_frame_count++;`) inside the ISC DMA-done IRQ handler. **2. Read API for decoupled producers:**
Producers outside the video task use `Video_GetFrameInfo()` (video.c:397–405), which reads `ISC_Capture_FrameCount()` (isc_capture.h:15). The read is **not lock-protected** — it's a bare `volatile uint32_t` (isc_capture.c:30, implied). On Cortex-A5 (32-bit MCU), naturally-aligned u32 reads are atomic. The accessor pattern is synchronous; each caller fetches the *current* value at call-time, not "the last notified value."

**3. Update cadence pattern:**
At 60 Hz video / 240 Hz fretboard samples, the same `frame_epoch` will indeed tag ~4 consecutive fretboard ADC records. **This is the expected pattern.** The spec (§4.2) and timing_pipeline (timing_pipeline.c:353–391) confirm: `frame_epoch` represents "most-recent video frame at the time the producer sampled." timing_pipeline is the closest precedent — it's decoupled from the detector-state bus, consumes detector events asynchronously (timing_pipeline.c:405: `xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS))`), and tags each PERF_REC_TIMING with the *detector's* `state->frame_epoch`, which may be stale relative to the live frame counter. This confirms: `frame_epoch` is "the frame at context-switch time," not a time-local per-sample tag.

**4. Other timing signal on each record:**
`ts_counter` (SYS_TIME raw counter, 64-bit) is **stamped by the perf-log API**, not the producer. Every `hdr_fill()` call (perf_log.c:115–123) runs `h->ts_counter = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()` at record-emit time. This gives sub-frame alignment for free: N fretboard ADC records sharing the same `frame_epoch` will have distinct `ts_counter` values (microsecond resolution implied by SYS_TIME). Host divides by `timer_freq_hz` (perf_rec_session_t) to convert to absolute time.

294	    float      color_target_b[FRET_COUNT];     /* per-fret target weights */
295	    float      color_target_g[FRET_COUNT];
296	    float      color_target_r[FRET_COUNT];
297	    float      color_reject_b[FRET_COUNT];     /* per-fret reject weights */
298	    float      color_reject_g[FRET_COUNT];
299	    float      color_reject_r[FRET_COUNT];
300	} perf_rec_detector_config_t;
301	
302	/* PERF_REC_ACTUATOR — emitted on every FretboardLink_Send call (i.e. on
303	 * intent), one record per call. Closes the gap between TIMING.publish_mask
304	 * (intent on the timing pipeline side) and FBL_SEND STAMP (a byte hit the
305	 * USB DMA): with multiple producers (timing_pipeline, manual_control, future
306	 * game_state_controller per spec §4.8), the wire byte alone doesn't say
307	 * who asserted what.
308	 *
309	 * intended_mask: what the producer asked for this Send (low 7 bits).
310	 * asserted_mask: what's currently held on the link (last byte queued).
311	 * strum_dir: from the bit pattern (0=none, 1=down, 2=up).
312	 * producer_id: perf_actuator_producer_t — the arbitration signal that's
313	 *              invisible on the wire today.
314	 * last_ack_*:  most recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE result and timestamp,
315	 *              snapshotted at Send-time so the host can compute transport-
316	 *              side latency without joining FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE
317	 *              stamps (still useful, but redundant for the common case). */
318	typedef enum
319	{
320	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_NONE   = 0,
321	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING = 1,
322	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_MANUAL = 2,
323	} perf_actuator_producer_t;
324	
325	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
326	{
327	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
328	    uint8_t    intended_mask;
329	    uint8_t    asserted_mask;
330	    uint8_t    strum_dir;            /* 0=none, 1=down, 2=up */
331	    uint8_t    producer_id;          /* perf_actuator_producer_t */
332	    int32_t    last_ack_result;      /* USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_*, signed for safety */
333	    uint64_t   last_ack_ts_counter;  /* SYS_TIME at most-recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE */
334	} perf_rec_actuator_t;
335	
336	/* ─── Host→device commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
337	 *
338	 * Wrapped in the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer as TX records. Magic is distinct
339	 * from PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC so a misrouted record frame can't be parsed as
340	 * a command (or vice versa). The device reads commands on the CDC OUT
341	 * endpoint; the host writes them via marvin-perf's set-mask path. */
342	
343	#define PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC   0x4D43u   /* 'M','C' little-endian */
344	
345	typedef enum
346	{
347	    PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK = 0x01u,
348	} perf_cmd_t;
349	
350	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
351	{
352	    uint16_t magic;        /* PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC */
353	    uint8_t  cmd_id;       /* perf_cmd_t */
354	    uint8_t  reserved;
355	} perf_cmd_hdr_t;
356	
357	/* PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK — bit i (i = perf_rec_type_t value) gates record
358	 * type i. SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask so the host can
359	 * still derive timer_freq_hz on attach. */
360	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
361	{
362	    perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr;
363	    uint32_t       enabled_mask;
364	} perf_cmd_set_mask_t;
365	
366	#endif /* PERF_LOG_RECORDS_H */
367

27	 * when it falls below CV_HOLD_THRESH × CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC. Per-color
28	 * edge thresholds are uniform at 50 by default — separable later if any
29	 * fret needs its own. Mirrors fret-tuner detect_video.py defaults. */
30	#define CV_HOLD_THRESH         100.0f
31	#define CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC   0.78f
32	#define CV_EDGE_THRESH         25.0f

36	/* Sensor coordinates in native capture-frame space, anchored to 720×480
37	 * (Wii 480p60 — primary production source). (hx,hy) = brightness sensor,
38	 * (ex,ey) = color-filtered edge sensor; both above the strike line.
39	 * Derived from fret-tuner detect_video.py 1920×1080 defaults via the
40	 * same Elgato HDMI capture, scaled by (3/8, 4/9). Runtime calibration
41	 * UI lands with M6. */
42	typedef struct { uint16_t hx, hy, ex, ey; } sensor_xy_t;
43	
44	static const sensor_xy_t s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT] =
45	{
46	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { 280, 311, 293, 311 },
47	    [FRET_RED]    = { 317, 311, 330, 311 },

49	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 393, 311, 380, 311 },
50	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { 430, 311, 417, 311 },

53	/* Per-fret BGR target / reject weights. Edge signal is
54	 * (target·c − max(0, reject·c)) × sat_ratio. Reject totals exceed 1.0
55	 * so camera-captured whites with color-temperature bias get suppressed,
56	 * not just mathematically perfect whites. */
57	typedef struct { float target[3]; float reject[3]; } color_filter_t;
58	
59	static const color_filter_t s_color_filter[FRET_COUNT] =
60	{
61	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.0f, 0.7f } },
62	    [FRET_RED]    = { { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.7f, 0.0f } },
63	    [FRET_YELLOW] = { { 0.0f, 0.5f, 0.5f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
64	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { { 1.0f, 0.4f, 0.0f }, { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.4f } },
65	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { { 0.0f, 0.3f, 0.7f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
66	};

68	/* Per-fret detector state. Private — not on the bus. press_count is the
69	 * rising-edge counter the strum scheduler will eventually consume. */
70	static float    s_hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];
71	static float    s_edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];
72	static bool     s_pressed[FRET_COUNT];
73	static bool     s_edge_active[FRET_COUNT];
74	static uint32_t s_press_count[FRET_COUNT];
75	
76	static StaticQueue_t s_frame_queue_buf;
77	static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(Video_FrameInfo)];
78	
79	static StackType_t   s_task_stack[CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS];

82	/* ─── Sampling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
83	
84	/* Average BGR over a (2r+1)×(2r+1) patch centered on (px,py), clipping
85	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration
86	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
87	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
88	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
89	{
90	    int cx = (int)px;
91	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
92	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
93	    int cy = (int)py;
94	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
95	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
96	
97	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
98	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
99	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
100	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
101	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
102	
103	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
104	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
105	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
106	    {
107	        const uint8_t *row = frame
108	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
109	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
110	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
111	        {
112	            sum_b += row[0];
113	            sum_g += row[1];
114	            sum_r += row[2];
115	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
116	        }
117	    }
118	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
119	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
120	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
121	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
122	}
123	
124	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
125	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
126	{
127	    float m = bgr[0];
128	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
129	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
130	    return m;
131	}
132	
133	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
134	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
135	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
136	{
137	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
138	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
139	    float cmin = bgr[0];
140	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
141	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
142	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
143	
144	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
145	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
146	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
147	    return (target - reject) * sat;
148	}
149	
150	/* ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
151	
152	static void detect_frame(const Video_FrameInfo *frame, QueueHandle_t bus)
153	{
154	    detector_state_t state;
155	    memset(&state, 0, sizeof(state));
156	    state.frame_epoch  = frame->frame_count;
157	    state.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK;
158	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
159	
160	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
161	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
162	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
163	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;
164	
165	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
166	    {
167	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
168	        float hold_bgr[3], edge_bgr[3];
169	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.hx, s.hy, hold_bgr);
170	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
171	
172	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);
173	        float ed = color_signal(edge_bgr, &s_color_filter[i]);
174	        s_hold_dist[i] = hd;
175	        s_edge_dist[i] = ed;
176	
177	        if (!s_pressed[i] && hd > CV_HOLD_THRESH)   { s_pressed[i] = true;  }
178	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
179	
180	        bool edge_on = ed > CV_EDGE_THRESH;
181	        if (edge_on && !s_edge_active[i]) { s_press_count[i]++; }
182	        s_edge_active[i] = edge_on;
183	
184	        state.fret[i].pressed = s_pressed[i] ? 1u : 0u;
185	
186	        /* confidence: edge_dist scaled to 0..65535. ed lives roughly in
187	         * channel-value units (~0..255) so ×256 fills the range. */
188	        float c = ed * 256.0f;
189	        if (c < 0.0f)        { c = 0.0f;     }
190	        if (c > 65535.0f)    { c = 65535.0f; }
191	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
192	
193	        /* raw_value: hold_dist (max channel, 0..255). */
194	        float h = hd;
195	        if (h < 0.0f)        { h = 0.0f;     }
196	        if (h > 65535.0f)    { h = 65535.0f; }
197	        state.fret[i].raw_value = (uint16_t)h;
198	    }
199	
200	    (void)xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0);
201	}
202	
203	/* ─── Calibration overlay ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
204	
205	/* Paints a per-fret ring at each sample point on the just-sampled frame so
206	 * the user can visually verify alignment with on-screen note targets. The
207	 * ring radius is outside the 5×5 sample patch — overdrawing here would
208	 * not affect *this* frame's reads (detect_frame already ran) but a future
209	 * re-sample on the same ring slot must still see clean source pixels. */
210	#define CV_OVERLAY_RING_R    4u
211	
212	static const uint8_t s_overlay_hold_bgr[3] = { 255u, 255u, 255u };  /* white */
213	static const uint8_t s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3] =
214	{   /* { B,    G,    R } */
215	    [FRET_GREEN]  = {   0u, 255u,   0u },
216	    [FRET_RED]    = {   0u,   0u, 255u },
217	    [FRET_YELLOW] = {   0u, 255u, 255u },
218	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 255u,   0u,   0u },
219	    [FRET_ORANGE] = {   0u, 165u, 255u },
220	};
221	
222	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
223	                                 int x, int y,
224	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
225	{
226	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
227	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
228	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
229	}
230	
231	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
232	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
233	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
234	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
235	{
236	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
237	    while (x >= y)
238	    {
239	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
240	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
241	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
242	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
243	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
244	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
245	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
246	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
247	        y++;
248	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
249	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
250	    }
251	}
252	
253	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
254	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
255	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
256	{
257	    int rr = radius * radius;
258	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
259	    {
260	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
261	        {
262	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
263	            {
264	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
265	            }
266	        }
267	    }
268	}
269	
270	/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching
271	 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
272	 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
273	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
274	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
275	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
276	#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u
277	
278	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh)
279	{
280	    int w = (int)fw, h = (int)fh;
281	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
282	    {
283	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
284	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
285	
286	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
287	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
288	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
289	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
290	
291	        if (s_pressed[i])
292	        {
293	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
294	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
295	        }
296	        if (s_edge_active[i])
297	        {
298	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
299	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
300	        }
301	    }
302	}

304	/* ─── Detector-config publish ──────────────────────────────────────────── */
305	
306	/* Snapshot the static cv_marvin_v1 tables (sample coords, thresholds,
307	 * color filter weights) into a wire record. Static today; when M6
308	 * calibration UI lands and these become runtime-tunable, this function
309	 * is the single point that re-publishes after each tweak. */
310	static void publish_detector_config(void)
311	{
312	    perf_rec_detector_config_t cfg;
313	    memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
314	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
315	    {
316	        cfg.sensor_hx[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].hx;
317	        cfg.sensor_hy[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].hy;
318	        cfg.sensor_ex[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].ex;
319	        cfg.sensor_ey[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].ey;
320	        cfg.color_target_b[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[0];
321	        cfg.color_target_g[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[1];
322	        cfg.color_target_r[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[2];
323	        cfg.color_reject_b[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[0];
324	        cfg.color_reject_g[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[1];
325	        cfg.color_reject_r[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[2];
326	    }
327	    cfg.hold_thresh       = CV_HOLD_THRESH;
328	    cfg.hold_release_frac = CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
329	    cfg.edge_thresh       = CV_EDGE_THRESH;
330	    PerfLog_EmitDetectorConfig(&cfg);
331	}

333	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
334	
335	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
336	{
337	    (void)param;
338	
339	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
340	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
341	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
342	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
343	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
344	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
345	    configASSERT(subscribed);
346	
347	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
348	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
349	
350	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
351	
352	    publish_detector_config();
353	
354	    for (;;)
355	    {
356	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
357	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
358	
359	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
360	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
361	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
362	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
363	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
364	
365	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
366	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
367	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
368	
369	        /* Re-emit detector config at ~1 Hz so a mid-stream host attach
370	         * picks it up within a second of frames flowing. Cheap (~188 B/s
371	         * × 1 record/s). When config becomes runtime-tunable, this becomes

18	 * visible at the configured window. You can run capture without display
19	 * (frames flow into DDR, BASE/UI fills the panel) or display without
20	 * capture (HEO shows whatever is in the framebuffer — possibly stale).
21	 *
22	 * Defaults at Initialize: capture disabled, display hidden, window
23	 * unset. Layout is app policy — DisplayShow is a no-op until the
24	 * caller has set a window with Video_SetWindow. */
25	
26	void Video_Initialize(void);

32	void Video_CaptureDisable(void);

43	 * within the panel. Takes effect on the next display bind (next
44	 * DisplayShow call, or when capture/lock state changes). */
45	void Video_SetWindow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h);

51	    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
52	    uint16_t width;

59	 * each time a frame completes to DDR — fanned out to every subscribed

61	 *   QueueHandle_t q = xQueueCreate(N, sizeof(Video_FrameInfo));
62	 *
63	 * Per-subscriber depth chooses the back-pressure policy. Depth 1 means
64	 * "process most recent frame, drop the rest" — when a frame arrives and
65	 * the queue is full, the IRQ's xQueueSendFromISR returns errQUEUE_FULL
66	 * and the frame is dropped for that subscriber. Deeper queues preserve
67	 * frames at the cost of memory and added latency. Each subscriber chooses
68	 * independently.

71	 * completed (one of the descriptor-ring slots). With NUM_BUFFERS > 2 a
72	 * subscriber can hold the pointer for multiple frame-times before the
73	 * ring laps it; with NUM_BUFFERS = 2 the buffer is overwritten on the
74	 * second-next frame.

78	 * concurrent subscribers (currently 4). */

181	static void on_frame_done(uint32_t frame_count,
182	                          uint32_t buffer_addr,
183	                          uintptr_t ctx)
184	{
185	    (void)ctx;
186	
187	    BaseType_t higher_priority_task_woken = pdFALSE;
188	    PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(PERF_STAGE_ISC_IRQ, frame_count, 0u,
189	                             &higher_priority_task_woken);
190	
191	    s_latest_buffer = buffer_addr;
192	
193	    /* Re-point HEO at the buffer that was just completed so the panel sees
194	     * every captured frame. With the descriptor ring and a static base
195	     * binding, HEO would only see frames written to slot 0. The address
196	     * latches at next vsync (XLCDC update=true); HEO and ISC run on
197	     * independent clocks so this is fine. Skip when display is hidden. */
198	    if (s_display_bound)
199	    {
200	        XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, buffer_addr, true);
201	    }
202	
203	    Video_FrameInfo info =
204	    {
205	        .buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)buffer_addr,
206	        .frame_count     = frame_count,
207	        .width           = s_src_w,
208	        .height          = s_src_h,
209	        .bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL,
210	    };
211	
212	    uint32_t subscriber_mask = 0u;
213	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
214	    {
215	        QueueHandle_t q = s_subscribers[i];
216	        if (q != NULL)
217	        {
218	            (void)xQueueSendFromISR(q, &info, &higher_priority_task_woken);
219	            subscriber_mask |= (1u << i);
220	        }
221	    }
222	    PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(PERF_STAGE_VIDEO_PUBLISH, frame_count,
223	                             subscriber_mask, &higher_priority_task_woken);
224	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(higher_priority_task_woken);
225	}
226	
227	/* ─── Capture state machine ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
228	
229	static bool capture_arm(void)
230	{
231	    uint16_t w = 0, h = 0;
232	    if (!TC358743_GetDetectedFormat(&w, &h)) { return false; }
233	
234	    if (!ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)) { return false; }
235	    s_src_w = w;
236	    s_src_h = h;
237	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(true);
238	    if (!ISC_Capture_Start())
239	    {
240	        (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
241	        return false;
242	    }
243	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture ARMED %ux%u\r\n", w, h);
244	    return true;
245	}
246	
247	static void capture_disarm(void)
248	{
249	    ISC_Capture_Stop();
250	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
251	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture IDLE\r\n");
252	}
253	
254	/* Bind/unbind display from current intent + most-recent source size +
255	 * caller-set window. A zero-sized window means the app hasn't set one
256	 * yet — silently skip the bind in that case rather than emit a malformed
257	 * HEO geometry; DisplayShow without a prior SetWindow is a no-op. */
258	static void display_apply(void)
259	{
260	    window_t w = s_window;
261	    bool window_valid = (w.w != 0u) && (w.h != 0u);
262	    bool source_valid = (s_src_w != 0u) && (s_src_h != 0u);
263	    bool want = s_display_shown && source_valid && window_valid;
264	
265	    if (want && !s_display_bound)
266	    {
267	        lcd_bind(s_src_w, s_src_h, w.x, w.y, w.w, w.h);
268	        s_display_bound = true;
269	    }
270	    else if (!want && s_display_bound)
271	    {
272	        lcd_unbind();
273	        s_display_bound = false;
274	    }
275	}
276	
277	/* Each tick: align current chain state (capture armed / display bound) to
278	 * the user's intent flags, given the current source-lock state. */
279	static void reconcile(void)
280	{
281	    bool locked = TC358743_IsLocked();
282	
283	    /* Capture: armed iff intent + lock. */
284	    bool want_capture = s_capture_enabled && locked;
285	    if (want_capture && !s_capture_armed)
286	    {
287	        if (capture_arm()) { s_capture_armed = true; }
288	    }
289	    else if (!want_capture && s_capture_armed)
290	    {
291	        capture_disarm();
292	        s_capture_armed = false;
293	    }
294	
295	    /* Display: shown iff intent + we have a source size to work with. The
296	     * source size is captured at arm time and persists across capture
297	     * teardown so the user can leave HEO bound on a stale frame. */
298	    display_apply();
299	}
300	
301	/* ─── Task body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
302	
303	static void video_task(void *param)
304	{
305	    (void)param;
306	
307	    /* One-time init in task context (scheduler running, so synchronous I²C
308	     * and SYS_TIME work). Brings up capture pipeline, TC358743 bridge,
309	     * backlight, and parks the panel in UI-only mode. */
310	    ISC_Capture_Initialize();
311	    ISC_Capture_SetFrameCallback(on_frame_done, 0);
312	    TC358743_Initialize();
313	    XLCDC_EnableBacklight();
314	    lcd_unbind();
315	
316	    for (;;)
317	    {
318	        TC358743_Tasks();
319	        reconcile();
320	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_POLL_MS));
321	    }
322	}
323	
324	/* ─── Public API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
325	
326	static StackType_t  s_task_stack[VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
327	static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
328	
329	void Video_Initialize(void)
330	{
331	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(video_task,
332	                                       "VideoTask",
333	                                       VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
334	                                       NULL,
335	                                       VIDEO_TASK_PRIORITY,
336	                                       s_task_stack,
337	                                       &s_task_tcb);
338	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_VIDEO, h);
339	}
340	
341	void Video_CaptureEnable(void)  { s_capture_enabled = true;  }
342	void Video_CaptureDisable(void) { s_capture_enabled = false; }
343	
344	void Video_DisplayShow(void)    { s_display_shown = true;    }
345	void Video_DisplayHide(void)    { s_display_shown = false;   }
346	
347	void Video_SetWindow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
348	{
349	    window_t w = { x, y, dst_w, dst_h };
350	    s_window = w;
351	    /* Force a re-bind on next reconcile if we're currently shown. */
352	    s_display_bound = false;
353	}
354	
355	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
356	{
357	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
358	
359	    bool ok = false;
360	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
361	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
362	    {
363	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q) { ok = true; break; }     /* already in */
364	        if (s_subscribers[i] == NULL)
365	        {
366	            s_subscribers[i] = q;
367	            ok = true;
368	            break;
369	        }
370	    }
371	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
372	
373	    if (!ok) { LOG_ERROR("VIDEO: subscriber table full (max %u)\r\n",
374	                         (unsigned)VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS); }
375	    return ok;
376	}
377	
378	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
379	{
380	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
381	
382	    bool ok = false;
383	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
384	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
385	    {
386	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q)
387	        {
388	            s_subscribers[i] = NULL;
389	            ok = true;
390	            break;
391	        }
392	    }
393	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
394	    return ok;
395	}
396	
397	void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info)
398	{
399	    if (info == NULL) { return; }
400	    info->buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)s_latest_buffer;
401	    info->frame_count     = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
402	    info->width           = s_src_w;
403	    info->height          = s_src_h;
404	    info->bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
405	}

204	
205	/* Paints a per-fret ring at each sample point on the just-sampled frame so
206	 * the user can visually verify alignment with on-screen note targets. The
207	 * ring radius is outside the 5×5 sample patch — overdrawing here would
208	 * not affect *this* frame's reads (detect_frame already ran) but a future
209	 * re-sample on the same ring slot must still see clean source pixels. */
210	#define CV_OVERLAY_RING_R    4u
211	
212	static const uint8_t s_overlay_hold_bgr[3] = { 255u, 255u, 255u };  /* white */
213	static const uint8_t s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3] =
214	{   /* { B,    G,    R } */
215	    [FRET_GREEN]  = {   0u, 255u,   0u },
216	    [FRET_RED]    = {   0u,   0u, 255u },
217	    [FRET_YELLOW] = {   0u, 255u, 255u },
218	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 255u,   0u,   0u },
219	    [FRET_ORANGE] = {   0u, 165u, 255u },
220	};
221	
222	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
223	                                 int x, int y,
224	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
225	{
226	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
227	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
228	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
229	}
230	
231	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
232	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
233	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
234	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
235	{
236	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
237	    while (x >= y)
238	    {
239	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
240	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
241	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
242	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
243	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
244	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
245	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
246	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
247	        y++;
248	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
249	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
250	    }
251	}
252	
253	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
254	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
255	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
256	{
257	    int rr = radius * radius;
258	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
259	    {
260	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
261	        {
262	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
263	            {
264	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
265	            }
266	        }
267	    }
268	}
269	
270	/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching
271	 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
272	 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
273	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
274	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
275	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
276	#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u
277	
278	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh)
279	{
280	    int w = (int)fw, h = (int)fh;
281	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
282	    {
283	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
284	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
285	
286	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
287	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
288	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
289	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
290	
291	        if (s_pressed[i])
292	        {
293	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
294	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
295	        }
296	        if (s_edge_active[i])
297	        {
298	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
299	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
300	        }
301	    }
302	}

353	static void process_frame(const detector_state_t *state)
354	{
355	    /* Detector frame timestamps drive the clock so this is replay-
356	     * deterministic. timestamp_us is monotonic per spec §4.2.3. */
357	    s_now_ms = (uint32_t)(state->timestamp_us / 1000ull);
358	    s_last_frame_us = state->timestamp_us;
359	
360	    uint8_t presses, releases, pressed_mask;
361	    derive_edges(state, &presses, &releases, &pressed_mask);
362	
363	    if (presses)
364	    {
365	        if (!s_chord_open)
366	        {
367	            s_chord_open     = true;
368	            s_chord_start_ms = s_now_ms;
369	            s_chord_mask     = 0u;
370	        }
371	        s_chord_mask |= presses;
372	    }
373	
374	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
375	    {
376	        if (releases & s_fret_bit[i])
377	        {
378	            s_release_at_ms[i]      = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
379	            s_release_pending_mask |= s_fret_bit[i];
380	        }
381	    }
382	
383	    advance(pressed_mask);
384	
385	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK, state->frame_epoch,
386	                      (uint32_t)s_output_mask);
387	
388	    perf_timing_snapshot_t snap;
389	    fill_timing_snapshot(&snap);
390	    PerfLog_EmitTiming(state->frame_epoch, &snap);
391	}
392	
393	static void timing_pipeline_task(void *param)
394	{
395	    (void)param;
396	
397	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
398	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
399	
400	    LOG_INFO("TIMING: pipeline started\r\n");
401	
402	    for (;;)
403	    {
404	        detector_state_t state;
405	        if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
406	        {
407	            if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
408	            {
409	                continue;
410	            }
411	            process_frame(&state);
412	        }
413	        else
414	        {
415	            /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
416	             * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
417	            s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
418	            advance(s_prev_pressed_mask);
419	        }
420	    }
421	}

```text
1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over USB CDC, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35	
36	### 1.4 What's done, what's next
37	
38	| Subsystem | Status |
39	|---|---|
40	| HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR, BGR888 packed) | ✅ working at 480p60 and 720p60. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md). |
41	| Display path (DDR → XLCDC HEO → LVDSC → panel) | ✅ working, pillarboxed/letterboxed, per-frame pointer swap. See [`display_path.md`](display_path.md). |
42	| FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, OSAL I²C | ✅ landed. |
43	| Lightweight log shim, FreeRTOS analytics, task priorities | ✅ done. |
44	| CV detection pipeline | 🚧 M1 complete: `cv_marvin_v1` running on captured frames, `detector_state_t` bus active. No actuation path through detector yet. §4.2. |
45	| Fretboard link (USB CDC host over EDBG) | ✅ working; commands flowing, gameplay tested. §4.3. |
46	| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO, strum) | ✅ working; end-to-end gameplay tested on Expert and Easy. §4.4. |
47	| Operator UI (Legato) | 🚧 Manual-control surface (8 buttons, Legato Composer) done; full calibration/log UI not started. §4.5, open Q5. |
48	| Reference-data recording & export (SD) | 🚧 SD recording not started. Perf-log USB CDC export (separate dev-tooling path) complete at 2.77 MB/s. §4.6, open Q1/Q2. |
49	| System services (config, time, watchdog) | 🚧 Partial: logging, FreeRTOS analytics, static task priorities done; config persistence and watchdog not started. §4.7. |
50	| Game-state awareness & high-level game control | 🚧 not started. §4.8, open Q10/Q11. |
51	
52	---
53	
54	## 2. System context
55	
56	### 2.1 Three-tier system
57	
58	```

122	
123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
```

400	
401	#### 4.8.1 Role
402	
403	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
404	
405	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
406	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
407	
408	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
409	
410	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
411	
412	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
413	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
414	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
415	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
416	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
417	
418	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
419	
420	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
421	
422	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
423	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
424	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
425	
426	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
427	
428	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
429	
430	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
431	
432	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
433	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
434	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
435	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
436	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
437	
438	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
439	
440	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
441	
442	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
443	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.

Perfect. Now I have the complete picture. Let me write a comprehensive report:

---

## Fretboard Link RX State: Current Assessment

**1. RX State Today: Write-Only**

The fretboard link is strictly **write-only**. Zero RX infrastructure:
- No `USB_HOST_CDC_Read()` calls anywhere in marvin
- No `READ_COMPLETE` event handler (fretboard_link.c:78–123 only handles WRITE_COMPLETE, SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE, SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE, DEVICE_DETACHED — line 119–120 default case is a silent no-op)
- No RX buffers declared (DMA or otherwise)
- The USB IN endpoint exists by default (part of CDC spec) but is never polled or consumed; bytes from the fretboard flow to the bus and disappear

**2. CDC Read API Surface**

The canonical signature (usb_host_cdc.h:881–887):
```c
USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT USB_HOST_CDC_Read(
    USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE * transferHandle,
    void * data,
    size_t size
);
```

Internally (usb_host_cdc.c:1521) it maps to `USB_HOST_DeviceTransfer(cdcInstance->bulkInPipeHandle, ...)`, so the stack handles DMA and IRQ automatically. Completion fires `USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE` with a data structure containing `transferHandle`, `result`, and `length` (usb_host_cdc.h:304–317).

**Invocation pattern** (no example in marvin yet, but standard):
- Call `USB_HOST_CDC_Read(handle, &transfer_handle, buffer, size)` → returns SUCCESS or error
- ISR signals `USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE` when done
- Handler retrieves buffer contents and `length` from event data
- One-shot: must re-issue `USB_HOST_CDC_Read()` to poll again

**3. Task Structure**

- Task: `fretboard_link_task()` (line 219–250), priority 5, 768-word stack
- **Current loop body**: 
  - Poll `s_cmd_queue` with `pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)` (50 ms timeout, line 236)
  - If cmd received: latch it as `last_mask`; else repeat `last_mask`
  - If connected: call `send_one_byte(mask)` (line 247)
  - Loop continues
- **RX parse loop**: most natural fit is **separate callback-driven task** (dedicated RX consumer) or **integrated callback into same task via queue push** (ISR handler → queue → same FBL task polls for both TX cmds and RX frames). One-shot read semantics argue against blocking loop; callback-rearm pattern is cleaner.

**4. CDC Event Handler Today**

- Defined: fretboard_link.c:78–123
- **Handled events**:
  - `USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE` (line 88–100): snapshot result + timestamp, signal semaphore
  - `USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE` (line 101–107): signal semaphore (setup only)
  - `USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE` (line 101–107): signal semaphore (setup only)
  - `USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_DEVICE_DETACHED` (line 109–117): mark disconnected, wake writer
- **Not handled**: `USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE` and `USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_SERIAL_STATE_NOTIFICATION_RECEIVED` fall into the `default` case (line 119–120), which is silent no-op

**5. Buffer/State Lifecycle**

- **No pre-allocated RX buffers** declared in fretboard_link.c or elsewhere
- **USB stack behavior**: one-shot read (must re-issue `USB_HOST_CDC_Read()` after each completion to receive next packet). No auto-rearm; stack is passive until app calls Read again.

---

**Natural seams for RX consumer**: Add `READ_COMPLETE` case to `cdc_event_handler`, allocate a 12-byte RX buffer (or ring of N frames), queue parsed frame data to consuming task(s), and spawn re-reads in the callback.

## Report: `frame_epoch` Alignment Token Analysis

**1. frame_epoch source & increment site:**
`frame_epoch` is `ISC_Capture.g_frame_count` directly. Increment happens in **firmware/marvin/default/src/video/isc_capture.c:62** (`g_frame_count++;`) inside the ISC DMA-done IRQ handler. The video module (via `on_frame_done()` at video.c:181–225) immediately publishes this to all frame subscribers and perf-log. **Publisher:** ISC hardware IRQ firing at capture rate (60 Hz).

**2. Read API for decoupled producers:**
Producers outside the video task use `Video_GetFrameInfo()` (video.c:397–405), which reads `ISC_Capture_FrameCount()` (isc_capture.h:15). The read is **not lock-protected** — it's a bare `volatile uint32_t` (isc_capture.c:30, implied). On Cortex-A5 (32-bit MCU), naturally-aligned u32 reads are atomic. The accessor pattern is synchronous; each caller fetches the *current* value at call-time, not "the last notified value."

**3. Update cadence pattern:**
At 60 Hz video / 240 Hz fretboard samples, the same `frame_epoch` will indeed tag ~4 consecutive fretboard ADC records. **This is the expected pattern.** The spec (§4.2) and timing_pipeline (timing_pipeline.c:353–391) confirm: `frame_epoch` represents "most-recent video frame at the time the producer sampled." timing_pipeline is the closest precedent — it's decoupled from the detector-state bus, consumes detector events asynchronously (timing_pipeline.c:405: `xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS))`), and tags each PERF_REC_TIMING with the *detector's* `state->frame_epoch`, which may be stale relative to the live frame counter. This confirms: `frame_epoch` is "the frame at context-switch time," not a time-local per-sample tag.

**4. Other timing signal on each record:**
`ts_counter` (SYS_TIME raw counter, 64-bit) is **stamped by the perf-log API**, not the producer. Every `hdr_fill()` call (perf_log.c:115–123) runs `h->ts_counter = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()` at record-emit time. This gives sub-frame alignment for free: N fretboard ADC records sharing the same `frame_epoch` will have distinct `ts_counter` values (microsecond resolution implied by SYS_TIME). Host divides by `timer_freq_hz` (perf_rec_session_t) to convert to absolute time.

**5. Subscriber bus & adc_fretboard scaffold:**
The detector-state bus is active (Detector_BusQueue, detector.c). `adc_fretboard` is **scaffolded but not implemented**: detector.h defines `DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1` enum entry (detector.h), the spec promises it at M2 (§8: "ADC stream ingested; `adc_fretboard` detector publishing onto the bus"). No `.c` file exists yet in firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/. The fretboard UART ingest path is TBD (spec §4.3: "ADC ingest — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector").

**Alignment path forward:** Fretboard ADC records can safely carry raw samples + `frame_epoch` from `Video_GetFrameInfo()` at the moment the UART task dequeues each 12-byte sample frame (240 Hz). `ts_counter` will distinguish the 4 records sharing one `frame_epoch` by ~4 ms apart. Both tokens support offline join on frame + sub-frame bins without ambiguity.
