1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over USB CDC, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35	
36	### 1.4 What's done, what's next
37	
38	| Subsystem | Status |
39	|---|---|
40	| HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR, BGR888 packed) | ✅ working at 480p60 and 720p60. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md). |
41	| Display path (DDR → XLCDC HEO → LVDSC → panel) | ✅ working, pillarboxed/letterboxed, per-frame pointer swap. See [`display_path.md`](display_path.md). |
42	| FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, OSAL I²C | ✅ landed. |
43	| Lightweight log shim, FreeRTOS analytics, task priorities | ✅ done. |
44	| CV detection pipeline | 🚧 M1 complete: `cv_marvin_v1` running on captured frames, `detector_state_t` bus active. No actuation path through detector yet. §4.2. |
45	| Fretboard link (USB CDC host over EDBG) | ✅ working; commands flowing, gameplay tested. §4.3. |
46	| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO, strum) | ✅ working; end-to-end gameplay tested on Expert and Easy. §4.4. |
47	| Operator UI (Legato) | 🚧 Manual-control surface (8 buttons, Legato Composer) done; full calibration/log UI not started. §4.5, open Q5. |
48	| Reference-data recording & export (SD) | 🚧 SD recording not started. Perf-log USB CDC export (separate dev-tooling path) complete at 2.77 MB/s. §4.6, open Q1/Q2. |
49	| System services (config, time, watchdog) | 🚧 Partial: logging, FreeRTOS analytics, static task priorities done; config persistence and watchdog not started. §4.7. |
50	| Game-state awareness & high-level game control | 🚧 not started. §4.8, open Q10/Q11. |
51	
52	---
53	
54	## 2. System context
55	
56	### 2.1 Three-tier system

122	
123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.
163	
164	---
165	
166	## 3. Hardware platform
167	
168	### 3.1 Boards and links
169	
170	| Board | Role | Connection to marvin |
171	|---|---|---|
172	| **SAM9X75 Curiosity** | marvin host (CPU, DDR, peripherals, panel/touch ports) | — |
173	| **Waveshare HDMI → CSI-2 adapter** (TC358743) | HDMI → MIPI CSI-2 bridge | I²C (FLEXCOM6, PA24/PA25, 400 kHz, addr `0x0F`) for control; 2-lane CSI-2 RX for data; PC15 PWD, PC19 RESET (currently unused — software reset over I²C). |
174	| **Microchip 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch** | Operator UI | LVDSC pair from XLCDC; I²C for maxtouch (existing Harmony driver). |
175	| **fretboard board** (PIC32CM6408PL10048) | Sensor + actuator MCU | USB CDC host (marvin is USB host to fretboard's on-board EDBG composite, VID=0x03EB PID=0x2175; CDC ACM bridged to SERCOM1 PB00/PB01 at 115 200 Bd). |
176	| **Wii guitar controller** | Physical input target | Open-drain GPIO on fretboard, not directly on marvin. |
177	| **(optional) dev PC** | Calibration / training-data ingest / replay viewer | SD card swap (primary) or USB CDC for live debug; no runtime dependency. |
178	
179	Pin assignments live in `firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/pin_configurations.csv`. The capture pipeline doc ([`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md)) is authoritative for CSI / ISC register state; the display path doc ([`display_path.md`](display_path.md)) is authoritative for XLCDC overlay wiring.
180	
181	### 3.2 SAM9X75 resources used / unused
182	
183	| Peripheral | Status | Notes |
184	|---|---|---|
185	| MIPI CSI-2 RX + ISC + CSI2DC | ✅ in use | 2 lanes, 972 Mbps/lane; BGR888 packed to DDR (CSI2DC RMS=1, 3 B/pixel). |
186	| XLCDC + LVDSC | ✅ in use | HEO layer, RGB\_888\_PACKED, per-frame pointer swap, pillarbox/letterbox. |

193	| USB host (EHCI + OHCI) | ✅ in use | Fretboard link — marvin is USB host to fretboard EDBG CDC. |
194	| USB device (UDPHS) | ✅ in use | Perf-log CDC ACM sink; marvin presents as USB device to dev PC, streams perf records at up to 2.77 MB/s. |
195	| Maxtouch I²C | 🚧 to be enabled | Operator UI (§4.5). |
196	| Watchdog | 🚧 not configured | System services (§4.7). |
197	| Free FLEXCOMs | several available | Fretboard UART link (§4.3) needs one. |

199	---
200	
201	## 4. Subsystems
202	
203	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
204	
205	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
206	
207	**What this subsystem owns:**
208	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
209	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
210	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
211	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
212	
213	**What it doesn't own:**
214	- CV processing (§4.2).
215	- Recording / export (§4.6).
216	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
217	
218	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
219	
220	#### 4.2.1 Role
221	
222	This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
223	
224	#### 4.2.2 Detector model
225	
226	A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:
227	
228	- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
229	- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate.
230	
231	Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.
232	
233	#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)
234	
235	```
236	typedef struct {
237	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
238	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
239	    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
240	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
241	    struct {
242	        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
243	        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
244	        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
245	    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
246	} detector_state_t;
247	```
248	
249	Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
250	
251	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
252	
253	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
254	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
255	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
256	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
257	
258	#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
259	
260	`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:
261	
262	- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
263	- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
264	- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
265	
266	#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
267	
268	- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
269	- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)
270	
271	### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅
272	
273	USB CDC host between marvin and the fretboard MCU. Marvin acts as USB host to the fretboard's on-board EDBG debugger (composite device exposing CDC ACM). EDBG bridges the CDC ACM interface to the fretboard's SERCOM1 UART at 500 000 Bd.
274	
275	- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). 1-byte bitmask, no framing.
276	- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 12-byte start/end-bracketed frame. Marvin's `fretboard_link` issues a continuously-rearming `USB_HOST_CDC_Read` and a sibling `fretboard_rx_task` parses each valid frame and republishes it as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
277	- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
278	
279	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
280	
281	Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:
282	
283	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
284	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
285	- Per-fret release scheduling.
286	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
287	- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.
288	
289	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.
290	
291	### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
292	
293	10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:
294	
295	- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
296	- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
297	- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
298	- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
299	
300	**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
301	
302	### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧
303	
304	#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)
305	
306	1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
307	2. **Replay / sanity check** — let the user (offline) scrub through a recorded session to investigate misses.
308	3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.
309	
310	Live off-device streaming for side-by-side comparison is *not* on the MVP critical path.
311	
312	#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card
313	
314	Recordings are persisted to an SD card via SDMMC + a simple filesystem (FAT32 via Harmony's FILE_SYSTEM service). The card is removed and read on a workstation; no live network path is required for MVP.
315	
316	Bandwidth ceiling: SDMMC sustained write ≥ 5 MB/s on Class-10 cards is reliably achievable. The recording format below is sized to land well below that.
317	
318	#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes
319	
320	A recording is a **directory** on the SD card, containing:
321	
322	```
323	recordings/
324	└── 2026-05-20T14-32-08/
325	    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
326	    ├── state.bin              // dense detector_state_t records, all detectors, all frames
327	    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
328	    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
329	    └── keyframes/
330	        ├── 000000.bgr         // raw BGR888 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
331	        ├── 000060.bgr
332	        └── ...
333	```
334	
335	- **`state.bin`** — append-only, fixed-size `detector_state_t` records (§4.2.3). At 60 Hz × 2 detectors × ~28 B = ~3.4 KB/s. Trivial.
336	- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
337	- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 12-byte frames at 240 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~2.9 KB/s. Modest. Until the SD recorder lands, the same data is available live as `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (28 B framed) in any marvin-perf capture (default-disabled; enable with `set-mask`).
338	- **Keyframes** — raw BGR888 packed dump every N captured frames. At 720×480 × 3 B = 1.04 MB/keyframe. Default cadence: **1 keyframe per second** (60-frame stride) → 1.04 MB/s sustained. Configurable (every 30 / 60 / 120 / 600 frames). At 1 fps a 5-minute session is ~312 MB — comfortable on any modern SD card.
339	- No software JPEG / video encode. SAM9X75 has no hardware JPEG; CPU encode at 60 fps is infeasible. Keyframes stay raw; offline tools can transcode if desired.
340	
341	Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.
342	
343	#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`
344	
345	A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.
346	
347	For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.
348	
349	#### 4.6.5 manifest.json
350	
351	Minimum fields:
352	
353	```json
354	{
355	  "schema_version": 1,
356	  "session_started_utc": "2026-05-20T14:32:08Z",
357	  "marvin_firmware_git": "<hash>",
358	  "capture": { "width": 720, "height": 480, "fps": 60, "format": "BGR888" },
359	  "keyframe_stride_frames": 60,
360	  "detectors": [
361	    { "id": "cv_marvin_v1", "version": "1.0.0", "calibration": { ... } },
362	    { "id": "adc_fretboard", "version": "1.0.0", "thresholds": { ... } }
363	  ],
364	  "timing": { "chord_window_ms": 20, "strum_delay_ms": 220, "fret_early_ms": 50, "strum_pulse_ms": 50 },
365	  "ended_utc": null
366	}
367	```
368	
369	Written at session start; `ended_utc` is patched on a clean stop.
370	
371	#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
372	
373	A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.04 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
374	
375	If the SD write FIFO falls behind (rare; only a sustained-throughput problem), the recorder drops keyframes (logs a `RECORD_DROP` event into `state.bin`'s metadata channel) but **never** drops detector-state records.
376	
377	#### 4.6.7 Off-board detectors recording independently
378	
379	When a future Edge-AI detection unit is brought online, it can:
380	
381	- Subscribe to marvin's `frame_epoch` over a chosen link (UART/Ethernet/etc.).
382	- Record its own observations (e.g. its own sensor data + its own detector output) in its own format, *keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch`*.
383	- Be aligned post-hoc against marvin's reference recording during training.
384	
385	The spec does not constrain how off-board detectors store their data — only the sync contract (`frame_epoch` timeline) is canonical.
386	
387	### 4.7 System services 🚧
388	
389	Cross-cutting services not owned by any one subsystem:
390	
391	- **Logging** ✅ severity-filtered printf shim (commit `a79042f`).
392	- **Time** ✅ TC0 / SYS_TIME for OSAL.
393	- **Config persistence** 🚧 calibration values, mode toggles, last-used recording stride. Storage TBD (a config file on SD vs internal flash).
394	- **Watchdog** 🚧 not yet enabled.
395	- **OTA** ⚪ out of scope for now.
396	
397	### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
398	
399	Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
400	
401	#### 4.8.1 Role
402	
403	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
404	
405	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
406	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
407	
408	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
409	
410	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
411	
412	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
413	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
414	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
415	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
416	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
417	
418	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
419	
420	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
421	
422	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
423	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
424	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
425	
426	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
427	
428	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
429	
430	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
431	
432	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
433	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
434	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
435	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
436	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
437	
438	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
439	
440	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
441	
442	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
443	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
444	
445	---
446	
447	## 5. External interfaces 🚧
448	
449	To be expanded once §4.3 (fretboard wire protocol) is settled. Will document:
450	
451	- Marvin ↔ fretboard UART framing, byte-for-byte.
452	- Recording on-disk binary layouts (the `_t` structs from §4.2.3 and §4.6 in canonical form, including endianness).
453	- USB-CDC dev console framing (if any), Ethernet ref-data stream framing (if/when added).
454	
455	## 6. Operating modes 🚧
456	
457	Default model: independent toggles (matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split). Confirmed direction; concrete toggle list:
458	
459	| Toggle | Effect |
460	|---|---|
461	| `detect_enable` | CV + ADC detectors run; detector-state bus is active. |
462	| `marvin_timing_enable` | marvin's chord FIFO / strum scheduler runs. When off, fretboard runs its own pipeline (§4.4 fallback). |
463	| `actuate_enable` | Commands are actually sent to fretboard. When off, marvin computes commands but suppresses them (dry-run). |
464	| `record_enable` | Recording task writes to SD. |
465	| `game_observe_enable` | Game-state observer task runs; `xGameStateQueue` is active. |
466	| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |
467	
468	A handful of named composite modes (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record) are presets over these toggles. Replay specifically requires loading a prior recording from SD and playing detector-state events back through the timing pipeline against the original keyframes — UI affordance for that comes later.
469	
470	## 7. Build & deploy 🚧
471	
472	To be filled. Topics: MCC-clobbered files (which paths are safe to edit by hand vs. regenerate), `user.cmake` boundaries, flashing workflow, sequence of MCC steps to reproduce the project.
473	
474	## 8. Phasing & milestones 🚧
475	
476	Proposed order; each is a buildable demo:
477	
478	1. **M1 — Reference detector v0** (§4.2). One CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` to the bus. No actuation. Proves the bus and the detection task structure.
479	2. **M2 — Fretboard link** (§4.3). UART up; ADC stream ingested; `adc_fretboard` detector publishing onto the bus alongside `cv_marvin_v1`.
480	3. **M3 — Timing pipeline + actuation** (§4.4). Chord FIFO + strum scheduling; commands sent over UART; fretboard actuates. End-to-end play possible.
481	4. **M4 — Recording to SD** (§4.6). SDMMC + FAT mount; record task writes state/commands/ADC/keyframes during a session.
482	5. **M5 — Operator UI v0** (§4.5). Live view with overlays; mode toggles. UI framework decided here.
483	6. **M6 — Calibration UI** (§4.5). Per-fret ROI placement + threshold tuning on the device.
484	7. **M7 — Replay** (§6). Load a recording from SD, replay through the timing pipeline.
485	8. **M8 — Standalone-fretboard fallback** (§4.4). Marvin-disabled-pipeline mode validated.
486	9. **M9 — Game-state observer v0** (§4.8). Recognize main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score states; surface as `xGameStateQueue` events. No control yet.
487	10. **M10 — Game-state control v0** (§4.8). High-level verbs ("start single-player song X") drive menu navigation through the same fretboard link.
488	
489	Live-stream Ethernet, Edge-AI integration, and config-on-flash are post-M8.
490

46	# in; for STRIP-heavy streams it's much less, which is the desired shape.
47	_QUEUE_MAX = 512

50	@dataclass
51	class _State:
52	    port: str | None = None
53	    mask: int = 0xFFFFFFFF
54	    started_at: str | None = None
55	    framing_stats: FrameStats = field(default_factory=FrameStats)

68	class _LiveSession:
69	    """Process-singleton; mutex guards all field writes."""
70	
71	    def __init__(self) -> None:
72	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
73	        self._state = _State()
74	        self._ser: SerialSource | None = None
75	        self._thread: threading.Thread | None = None
76	        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
77	        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] | None = None
78	        self._loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop | None = None
79	        self._ws: WebSocket | None = None
80	        self._rec: _Recording | None = None
81	        # Late-bound to avoid a cycle: api.py passes this on import.
82	        self._record_to_dict = None  # type: ignore[var-annotated]
83	
84	    # ─── lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
85	
86	    def configure(self, *, record_to_dict) -> None:
87	        self._record_to_dict = record_to_dict
88	
89	    def is_active(self) -> bool:
90	        with self._lock:
91	            return self._thread is not None and self._thread.is_alive()
92	
93	    def start(self, port: str, *, ser_factory=None) -> None:
94	        """Open serial + start reader thread.
95	
96	        ``ser_factory`` is an injection point for tests — if provided, called
97	        as ``ser_factory(port)`` and expected to return a context-manager
98	        iterable (yields bytes chunks) with ``send_command``.
99	        """
100	        with self._lock:
101	            if self.is_active():
102	                raise RuntimeError("live session already active")
103	            self._stop_event.clear()
104	            self._state = _State(
105	                port=port,
106	                started_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
107	            )
108	            ser = (ser_factory or SerialSource)(port)
109	            ser.__enter__()
110	            self._ser = ser
111	            self._thread = threading.Thread(
112	                target=self._reader_loop,
113	                name="marvin-perf-live",
114	                daemon=True,
115	            )
116	            self._thread.start()
117	
118	    def stop(self) -> None:
119	        """Idempotent: safe to call when not active. Auto-finalizes any
120	        in-flight recording so the bin is openable from offline mode."""
121	        # Finalize first: while the reader is still alive, in-flight frames
122	        # land in the bin instead of being lost to the close race.
123	        try:
124	            self.record_stop()
125	        except Exception:
126	            pass
127	        with self._lock:
128	            self._stop_event.set()
129	            ser = self._ser
130	            self._ser = None
131	            t = self._thread
132	            self._thread = None
133	        if ser is not None:
134	            try:
135	                ser.__exit__(None, None, None)
136	            except Exception:
137	                pass
138	        if t is not None and t.is_alive():
139	            t.join(timeout=3.0)
140	
141	    # ─── control plane ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
142	
143	    def set_mask_from_int(self, mask: int) -> int:
144	        m = mask & 0xFFFFFFFF
145	        with self._lock:
146	            ser = self._ser
147	            if ser is None:
148	                raise RuntimeError("live session not active")
149	            self._state.mask = m
150	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_set_mask_payload(m)))
151	        # Drain the WS queue so the browser sees fresh records under the new
152	        # mask immediately, rather than draining 5–10 s of stale backlog.
153	        self._drain_queue()
154	        self._post("mask", {"value": f"0x{m:08x}", "source": "client"})
155	        return m
156	
157	    def set_mask_from_names(self, names: list[str]) -> int:
158	        mask = 0
159	        for raw in names:
160	            token = raw.strip().upper()
161	            if not token:
162	                continue
163	            if token == "ALL":
164	                mask = 0xFFFFFFFF
165	                break
166	            if token not in RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME:
167	                valid = ", ".join(sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME))
168	                raise ValueError(f"unknown record type {token!r}; valid: {valid}, ALL")
169	            mask |= 1 << RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME[token]
170	        return self.set_mask_from_int(mask)
171	
172	    def status(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
173	        with self._lock:
174	            active = self.is_active()
175	            return {
176	                "active": active,
177	                "port": self._state.port if active else None,
178	                "mask": f"0x{self._state.mask:08x}" if active else None,
179	                "recording": self._recording_dict_locked(),
180	                "started_at": self._state.started_at if active else None,
181	                "framing": {
182	                    "frames_ok": self._state.framing_stats.frames_ok,
183	                    "fcs_err": self._state.framing_stats.fcs_mismatches,
184	                    "resync_drop": self._state.framing_stats.bytes_resync_dropped,
185	                    "bad_lengths": self._state.framing_stats.bad_lengths,
186	                },
187	            }
188	
189	    def _recording_dict_locked(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
190	        rec = self._rec
191	        if rec is None:
192	            return None
193	        return {
194	            "capture_dir": str(rec.dir),
195	            "bytes_written": rec.bytes_written,
196	            "n_frames": rec.n_frames,
197	            "started_at": rec.started_at,
198	        }
199	
200	    # ─── recording ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201	
202	    def record_start(self, out_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
203	        """Open ``<out_dir>/perf.bin`` and start mirroring framed bytes.
204	
205	        Reader thread picks up the new ``self._rec`` on its next iteration
206	        and writes ``frame.framed`` per validated frame.
207	        """
208	        with self._lock:
209	            if not self.is_active():
210	                raise RuntimeError("live session not active")
211	            if self._rec is not None:
212	                raise RuntimeError("already recording")
213	            cap_dir = init_capture_dir(out_dir, exist_ok=False)
214	            bin_path = cap_dir / BIN_NAME
215	            fh = bin_path.open("wb")
216	            self._rec = _Recording(
217	                fh=fh,
218	                dir=cap_dir,
219	                started_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
220	            )
221	            snapshot = self._recording_dict_locked()
222	        self._post("recording", {"state": "started", **(snapshot or {})})
223	        return snapshot or {}
224	
225	    def record_stop(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
226	        """Idempotent. Closes the bin, writes manifest.json, returns the
227	        manifest summary. ``None`` if not recording."""
228	        with self._lock:
229	            rec = self._rec
230	            self._rec = None
231	            port = self._state.port
232	            session = self._state.last_session_dict
233	        if rec is None:
234	            return None
235	        stopped_at_dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
236	        stopped_at = stopped_at_dt.isoformat()
237	        try:
238	            started_at_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(rec.started_at)
239	            duration_s = (stopped_at_dt - started_at_dt).total_seconds()
240	        except Exception:
241	            duration_s = None
242	        try:
243	            rec.fh.flush()
244	        except Exception:
245	            pass
246	        try:
247	            rec.fh.close()
248	        except Exception:
249	            pass
250	        # Pull timer_freq_hz from the cached SESSION if we saw one on the
251	        # WS at any point. Bin-derived freq still wins inside synthesize.
252	        timer_freq_fallback = None
253	        if session is not None:
254	            try:
255	                timer_freq_fallback = int(session.get("timer_freq_hz"))
256	            except (TypeError, ValueError):
257	                timer_freq_fallback = None
258	        manifest_dict: dict[str, Any]
259	        try:
260	            manifest = finalize_capture_dir(
261	                rec.dir,
262	                source=CaptureSource(kind="serial", port=port or ""),
263	                timer_freq_hz_fallback=timer_freq_fallback,
264	                recording_started_at=rec.started_at,
265	                recording_stopped_at=stopped_at,
266	                recording_duration_s=duration_s,
267	            )
268	            manifest_dict = manifest.to_dict()
269	        except Exception as e:
270	            manifest_dict = {"error": str(e)}
271	        result = {
272	            "capture_dir": str(rec.dir),
273	            "bytes_written": rec.bytes_written,
274	            "n_frames": rec.n_frames,
275	            "manifest": manifest_dict,
276	        }
277	        self._post("recording", {"state": "stopped", **result})
278	        return result
279	
280	    # ─── WS attachment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
281	
282	    async def attach_ws(self, ws: WebSocket) -> None:
283	        with self._lock:
284	            if self._ws is not None:
285	                await ws.close(code=4409, reason="live already in use")
286	                return
287	            if not self.is_active():
288	                await ws.close(code=4404, reason="no active live session")
289	                return
290	            self._loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
291	            self._queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=_QUEUE_MAX)
292	            self._ws = ws
293	
294	        await ws.accept()
295	        with self._lock:
296	            hello = {
297	                "type": "hello",
298	                "session": {
299	                    "started_at": self._state.started_at,
300	                    "port": self._state.port,
301	                    "mask": f"0x{self._state.mask:08x}",
302	                    "recording": self._recording_dict_locked(),
303	                },
304	            }
305	            replay = self._state.last_session_dict
306	        try:
307	            await ws.send_json(hello)
308	            if replay is not None:
309	                await ws.send_json({"type": "session_replay", "rec": replay})
310	            queue = self._queue
311	            while True:
312	                msg_type, payload = await queue.get()
313	                if msg_type == "record":
314	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "record", "rec": payload})
315	                elif msg_type == "mask":
316	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "mask", **payload})
317	                elif msg_type == "error":
318	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "error", **payload})
319	                    break
320	                elif msg_type == "framing_stats":
321	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "framing_stats", **payload})
322	                elif msg_type == "recording":
323	                    await ws.send_json({"type": "recording", **payload})
324	        except WebSocketDisconnect:
325	            pass
326	        finally:
327	            with self._lock:
328	                self._ws = None
329	                self._queue = None
330	
331	    # ─── reader thread ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
332	
333	    def _reader_loop(self) -> None:
334	        ser = self._ser
335	        stats = self._state.framing_stats
336	        if ser is None:
337	            return
338	        try:
339	            for frame in iter_frames(ser, stats):
340	                if self._stop_event.is_set():
341	                    break
342	                self._mirror_to_recording(frame.framed)
343	                try:
344	                    rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
345	                except Exception:
346	                    continue
347	                if self._record_to_dict is None:
348	                    continue
349	                rec_dict = self._record_to_dict(rec, include_bgr=True)
350	                if isinstance(rec, Session):
351	                    with self._lock:
352	                        self._state.last_session_dict = rec_dict
353	                self._post("record", rec_dict)
354	        except Exception as e:
355	            self._post("error", {"code": "serial-error", "msg": str(e)})
356	        finally:
357	            # Reader exit (clean stop or serial error): finalize any
358	            # active recording so the bin is left in an openable state.
359	            try:
360	                self.record_stop()
361	            except Exception:
362	                pass
363	
364	    def _mirror_to_recording(self, framed: bytes) -> None:
365	        """Reader-thread tap: write validated framed bytes to the active
366	        recording, if any. Disable the recording on write failure rather
367	        than tear down the whole session."""
368	        with self._lock:
369	            rec = self._rec
370	            if rec is None:
371	                return
372	            try:
373	                rec.fh.write(framed)
374	                rec.bytes_written += len(framed)
375	                rec.n_frames += 1
376	                return
377	            except OSError as e:
378	                self._rec = None
379	                err_msg = str(e)
380	                fh = rec.fh
381	        try:
382	            fh.close()
383	        except Exception:
384	            pass
385	        self._post("error", {"code": "record-write", "msg": err_msg})
386	
387	    # ─── internal: cross-thread queue post ──────────────────────────────
388	
389	    def _post(self, msg_type: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
390	        loop = self._loop
391	        queue = self._queue
392	        if loop is None or queue is None:
393	            return
394	        try:
395	            loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._queue_put_nowait, msg_type, payload)
396	        except RuntimeError:
397	            pass
398	
399	    def _queue_put_nowait(self, msg_type: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
400	        # Runs on the asyncio loop thread (single producer/consumer here).
401	        # On overflow, drop the oldest item so the WS receiver always sees
402	        # the freshest data — useful when STRIP records swamp the link.
403	        if self._queue is None:
404	            return
405	        try:
406	            self._queue.put_nowait((msg_type, payload))
407	        except asyncio.QueueFull:
408	            try:
409	                self._queue.get_nowait()
410	            except asyncio.QueueEmpty:
411	                return
412	            try:
413	                self._queue.put_nowait((msg_type, payload))
414	            except asyncio.QueueFull:
415	                pass
416	
417	    def _drain_queue(self) -> None:
418	        loop = self._loop
419	        if loop is None:
420	            return
421	        try:
422	            loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._queue_drain)
423	        except RuntimeError:
424	            pass
425	
426	    def _queue_drain(self) -> None:
427	        if self._queue is None:
428	            return
429	        while True:
430	            try:
431	                self._queue.get_nowait()
432	            except asyncio.QueueEmpty:
433	                return
434	
435

81	        capture = open_capture(path)

99	            framing_stats=stats,

419	def _record_to_dict(rec: Record, *, include_bgr: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
420	    """Compact, JSON-friendly view of a record. Offline mode keeps strip
421	    pixels on the dedicated PNG endpoint; live mode passes ``include_bgr=True``
422	    so the WS push carries pixel bytes (base64) for client-side canvas render."""
423	    hdr = rec.hdr  # type: ignore[union-attr]
424	    base: dict[str, Any] = {
425	        "type": type(rec).__name__,
426	        "frame_epoch": hdr.frame_epoch,
427	        "ts_counter": hdr.ts_counter,
428	        "flags": hdr.flags,
429	    }
430	    if isinstance(rec, Session):
431	        base.update(
432	            timer_freq_hz=rec.timer_freq_hz,
433	            schema_version=rec.schema_version,
434	            fw_git_short=rec.fw_git_short,
435	        )
436	    elif isinstance(rec, Stamp):
437	        try:
438	            base["stage"] = Stage(rec.stage_id).name
439	        except ValueError:
440	            base["stage"] = f"stage_{rec.stage_id:#04x}"
441	        base["stage_id"] = rec.stage_id
442	        base["aux"] = rec.aux
443	    elif isinstance(rec, Drop):
444	        base.update(
445	            dropped_state=rec.dropped_state,
446	            dropped_strip=rec.dropped_strip,
447	            dropped_sink=rec.dropped_sink,
448	        )
449	    elif isinstance(rec, TaskHighwater):
450	        try:
451	            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
452	        except ValueError:
453	            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
454	        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
455	        base["words"] = rec.words
456	    elif isinstance(rec, TaskRuntime):
457	        try:
458	            base["task_name"] = TaskId(rec.task_id).name
459	        except ValueError:
460	            base["task_name"] = f"task_{rec.task_id}"
461	        try:
462	            base["state_name"] = TaskState(rec.state).name
463	        except ValueError:
464	            base["state_name"] = f"state_{rec.state}"
465	        base["task_id"] = rec.task_id
466	        base["state"] = rec.state
467	        base["priority"] = rec.priority
468	        base["run_time_counter"] = rec.run_time_counter
469	    elif isinstance(rec, Strip):
470	        base.update(
471	            x=rec.x, y=rec.y, w=rec.w, h=rec.h,
472	            kind=rec.kind, kind_name=rec.kind_name,
473	        )
474	        if include_bgr:
475	            import base64
476	            base["bgr_b64"] = base64.b64encode(rec.bgr).decode("ascii")
477	    else:
478	        # Detector, Timing, Actuator, DetectorConfig, UnknownRecord — generic
479	        # field projection. Use dataclasses.fields() rather than
480	        # __dataclass_fields__ so ClassVar entries (`_BODY`, `SIZE`) stay out
481	        # — `from __future__ import annotations` keeps them in the latter.
482	        if hasattr(rec, "__dataclass_fields__"):
483	            for f in dc_fields(rec):
484	                if f.name == "hdr":
485	                    continue
486	                v = getattr(rec, f.name)
487	                if isinstance(v, (bytes, bytearray)):
488	                    base[f.name] = f"<{len(v)} B>"
489	                elif isinstance(v, tuple):
490	                    base[f.name] = list(v)
491	                else:
492	                    base[f.name] = v
493	    return base

1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Current focus
8	
9	**M1 — Reference detector v0.** First CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` records onto the detector-state bus. No actuation yet. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.2 for subsystem detail and §8 for the milestone progression.
10	
11	Scaffold is in place as of 2026-05-20: `detector/detector.{h,c}` owns the bus queue + a temporary drain task that logs records-per-second; `detector/cv_marvin_v1.{h,c}` subscribes to the video frame queue and publishes one `detector_state_t` per frame with `frame_epoch = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count` and all-zero fret state. Next: pick the v0 algorithm (Q8) and start populating `fret[]`.
12	
13	**Capture/display pipeline is done as of 2026-05-02:** source → TC358743 → CSI-2 @ 972 Mbps/lane → SAM9X75 → ISC DMA → DDR (BGRX32) → XLCDC OVR1 → LVDSC → 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel.
14	
15	> **Deeper-dive references:**
16	> - [`spec.md`](spec.md) — system-level spec (read first).
17	> - [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) — HDMI → DDR capture stage (CSI2DC, ISC, register settings, datasheet citations).
18	> - [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) — DDR → LCD display stage (XLCDC OVR1 wiring, pillarbox, cache coherence).
19	
20	> **Earlier entries** (capture/display bring-up, 2026-05-01 → 2026-05-15) are preserved in [`journal-archive.md`](journal-archive.md).
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Decision log
25	
26	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
27	|------|----------|-----------|
28	| 2026-06-02 | New `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` record type (`0x0B`) + `PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX` task slot (17). Default-disabled at boot like the other high-rate types; host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`. `fretboard_link` gains a continuously-rearming `USB_HOST_CDC_Read` plus a sibling `fretboard_rx_task` that pops bytes off a 512 B stream buffer and emits one record per valid 12-byte fretboard data frame at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate. No `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump — additive only. | Step 1 of the Edge-AI training-dataset workstream: `cv_marvin_v1` provides the reference label per video frame, fretboard ADC samples are the input the future Edge-AI MCU would see. Routing both signals through the perf log lets one offline tool join them on `frame_epoch` (~4 fretboard records per video frame) and `ts_counter` (sub-frame ordering), which is the cheapest path to a labelled dataset before the SD recorder (§4.6) exists. Sibling task instead of folding RX into `fretboard_link_task` keeps the existing TX path untouched (its `xQueueReceive` blocking shape doesn't compose with a stream buffer without bigger surgery). The downstream `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2, M2) is the natural follow-up; the bus scaffold (`DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1`) is already reserved. |
29	| 2026-06-02 | `FBL_BAUDRATE` raised 115200 → 500000 in `actuator/fretboard_link.c`, comment rewritten to reflect the EDBG-CDC-bridge reality. | The fretboard PIC32 SERCOM1 was retuned to 500 000 baud (firmware/fretboard, 2026-06-02). The link rides the on-board EDBG USB-UART bridge, so the CDC SET_LINE_CODING value is what EDBG clocks out to the PIC32 — must match exactly or every byte is corrupt. The previous comment ("fretboard side ignores baud over USB CDC") was wrong; only matters that the *application* on the PIC32 doesn't see the CDC line-coding fields, but the EDBG bridge in between very much does. `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py` still hardcodes `ACTUATOR_BAUDRATE = 115200` for the same physical link — flagged as a follow-up; out of scope for this commit (different subproject). |
30	| 2026-06-01 | Perf-log v3 schema bump: add `DETECTOR_CONFIG` (cv_marvin_v1 sample coords/thresholds/color filters), `ACTUATOR` (intended/asserted masks + `producer_id` + ack timing), extend `TIMING` to a per-frame snapshot (chord window mask, note/strum queue head + deadlines, release timers, frets_active), and add `PERF_TASK_IDLE` + `PERF_TASK_OTHER` pseudo-slots so per-window CPU% adds to 100%. | Wire's job pivots from "prove bytes survived and the pipeline isn't dropping" (v1/v2 integrity story, complete) to "show the host what the detection algorithm and actuator are thinking" (tuning visibility). Bundling four additions into one schema cut avoids three rounds of firmware/host sync. Granular MCC-task breakdown deferred — not needed at this time. Causal-trace `TIMING_EVENT`, ISR latency histograms, Cortex-A5 PMU counters, free-heap reporting also out of scope this round. Plan details in 2026-06-01 session log entry. |
31	| 2026-05-29 | Patch the UDPHS device driver to arm DMA for queued IRPs in completion ISRs. New helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` called after queue advance in `Tasks_ISR_DMA` and the ZLP-completion path. Logged as patch #9. | Stock Harmony USB v3.16.0 driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch — IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in the linked list but never get armed for transmission. Without this, `queueSizeWrite > 1` accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch — we'd accept three perf-log strips, transmit one, the other two stranded forever. The IRP-queue infrastructure is *already there* in the driver, the missing piece is the post-completion arm. Fix is additive (new helper, two new call sites, no refactor of existing IRPSubmit body), making it easy to find/maintain after MCC regen. Future Harmony versions may obviate this if upstream wires it up. |
32	| 2026-05-29 | Strip queue uses 1-byte slot indices into a static `s_strip_pool[depth+2]` instead of pass-by-value `perf_rec_strip_t` items. | FreeRTOS queues are pass-by-value: every `xQueueSend`/`xQueueReceive` does `memcpy(slot, src, item_size)` inside a critical section (interrupts disabled). At `sizeof(perf_rec_strip_t) = 23-61 KB`, that was 38-100 µs of interrupts-off time per queue op × ~240 ops/s. Pool-and-index pattern moves the pixel data into a static pool indexed by 1-byte handles; queue ops drop to 1 µs critical sections. Same total BSS footprint (eliminates the producer's `static r;` and drain's `static s_strip_drain;` — pool size matches old "queue + 2 staging" footprint). Pool size `depth + 2` covers "1 slot in producer's hand + 1 in drain's hand" while preserving drop-on-full semantics. |
33	| 2026-05-29 | Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF) replaces CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE in the framing layer. `crc_*` field names renamed to `fcs_*` end-to-end. | USB hardware already CRCs every bulk packet on the wire; our framing-layer checksum's job is *firmware-side framing-bug detection* and *resync alignment* (false SOF in the middle of a corrupt stream). Fletcher-16 catches single-byte changes, adjacent swaps, and most non-adjacent swaps with ~1/65536 false-positive rate against random byte streams — sufficient for that job at ~2 cycles/byte (vs ~25 cycles for the bit-by-bit CRC, ~6 cycles for table-driven). SAM9X75 has no CRCCU peripheral (verified against `packs/SAM9X75D2G_DFP/component/`), so DMA-driven CRC isn't available. Wire format unchanged (still SOF+LEN+payload+16-bit checksum). One-shot wire-format break — old `.bin` captures aren't readable with new code; fine for dev. |
34	| 2026-05-29 | Single `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES = 65000u` constant; `PERF_STRIP_MAX_W`/`MAX_H` removed. | The W×H pair was arbitrary — producer code only ever checks total bytes (`w * h * BPP <= PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`). Real binding constraint is the wire LEN field, which is `uint16_t` → max 65535 byte payload → max ~65 KB pixel per strip. Tighter than the UDPHS DMA cap (128 KB at `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE = 2`). Picking 65000 lands just under the LEN cap with margin. Producer accepts any (w, h) shape under that — practical envelope at 60 fps: 720×30, 480×45, 320×64, 290×72. Going beyond requires bumping LEN to u32, which is a wire-format break and not worth doing casually since wire bandwidth caps out around the same point at 60 fps. |
35	| 2026-05-29 | Default-disable high-rate perf-log record types at firmware boot — start mask is `DROP | TASK_HIGHWATER | TASK_RUNTIME` only; STAMP, DETECTOR, TIMING, STRIP off until host enables. | Avoids the unattended-firmware case where boot generates multi-MB/s of strip records that all get dropped at the sink (no DTR), burning producer-side CPU on framing/Fletcher work that goes nowhere. Host viewer enables higher-rate types via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` on attach (the live mode's mask UI). SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask so the host gets `timer_freq_hz` on attach. |
36	| 2026-05-21 | `configMAX_PRIORITIES` bumped 5 → 8; tasks re-tiered into 4 active bands (UI=2, diagnostic+perf-wire=3, vision=4, strum-critical+host-wire=5) plus 3 reserve bands (1, 6, 7) and idle (0). MCC tasks re-prioritised via the per-component yml files so future regens preserve the layout. | Pre-change layout had 11 tasks bunched at priority 1 (9 MCC pollers + VideoTask + DetectorDrain) and 4 at priority 2, with no headroom. Two concrete problems: (a) VideoTask was *below* its consumer CvMarvinV1, a classic priority inversion that would bite during any priority-2 busy spell; (b) Legato (UI rendering) at the same priority as USB host driver tasks meant a heavy frame redraw could stall fretboard wire transit. The new layout puts strum-critical output above vision-real-time above diagnostic-I/O above UI, which matches the failure-cost ordering: a late strum is a missed note, a late detector tick recovers next frame, a late UI paint is jitter only. Reserve bands cost ~60 B BSS each, leave room for future watchdog or fault-recovery work to land without re-shuffling. Setting priorities in MCC yml (rather than patching `tasks.c` post-regen) avoids a re-apply patch — the source of truth and the emitted code now agree. |

Spec §4.4. (c) 1-byte bitmask matches `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py` and `firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h` exactly (G/R/Y/B/O at bits 0..4, strum-down bit 5, strum-up bit 6) — no reason to invent a new framing while the protocol is this small. Future paths considered: (1) marvin compensates by subtracting a fretboard-published latency from `assert_at`/`strum_at`; (2) fretboard compensates by accepting timestamped events and scheduling locally. 95	- **`vApplicationStackOverflowHook` is a silent infinite-loop.** ([freertos_hooks.c:62-76](../default/src/config/default/freertos_hooks.c#L62-L76)) MCC's default is `taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS()` then `for (;;)`. An actual overflow is indistinguishable from any other freeze on hardware. Patch the hook to emit a `LOG_ERR` line naming the offending task before the spin (carefully — the stack is already corrupt, so the hook should avoid using locals or large stack frames). Already nearly bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. (HWM/RUNTIME records reach the host now post-2026-05-29 work, so we have *steady-state* stack visibility — but a real overflow still freezes silently.)

103	- **MCC-file modifications maintenance risk.** A from-scratch MCC regen on 2026-05-15 confirmed **four** local modifications get clobbered. The 2026-05-20 USB-host regen added a fifth. Re-apply after every regen:
104	
105	  1. **`plib_csi.c` — `CSI_Analog_Init` refactor.** MCC emits per-lane HS-RX init inline with three bugs: Lane 1 in the 2-lane branch is missing the bit-rate write, Lane 2's lane-select code is `0x24` instead of `0x64`, and the 4-lane else-if branch skips Lane 1 entirely. Replace with the `csi_phy_hs_rx_init(lane_code, bit_rate)` helper and call it for lanes 0/1/2/3 from a flat `if (nlanes >= …)` chain.
106	
107	  2. **`plib_xlcdc.c` `XLCDC_EnableClocks` — `PMC_PLL_ACR`.** Set to datasheet-optimal `0x12023010` for the LVDSPLL with our 24 MHz reference (in the `fIN ∈ [20 MHz, 32 MHz]` band). Specifically: `LOOP_FILTER=0x12, LOCK_THR=0x2, UTMIBG=1, UTMIVR=1, CONTROL=0x10`. MCC's default emits a different (less-optimal) analog config (`LOOP_FILTER=0x1B, LOCK_THR=0x4, no UTMI bits`). Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.
108	
109	  3. **`plib_csi2dc.c` `CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe` — `| CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1`.** Required by the RGB888-packed capture path: byte-stream packs 4 BGR pixels across 12 bytes per CSI-2 RMS spec (Table 49.27). Without it, capture writes wrong-format bytes and the display shows garbage. *(Earlier journal note claimed this was now MCC's default — incorrect; this regen confirmed MCC still emits without RMS_1.)*
110	
111	  4. **`drv_image_sensor.h` enum shim.** MCC's regen *deletes* this file when the image-sensor component is disabled. Restore the 30-line shim at `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/image_sensor/drv_image_sensor.h` defining `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RAW_BAYER…JPEG` and `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT…40_BIT` enums (numeric values must match the original — `drv_isc.c` derives `bits_per_pixel = 4 - inputBits`). Without it, `drv_isc.c` and `configuration.h` won't compile.
112	
113	  5. **`initialization.c` `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` — per-pin VBUS calls.** MCC emits a single `VBUS_AH_*_Set/Clear()` call expecting one pin named `VBUS_AH`, but our config has VBUS on two pins (PC27 + PC31, one per USB port). The pin-macro generator produces `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_*` and `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_*` separately and no unified wrapper, so the MCC-emitted code fails to compile. Replace lines 162-163 (Set branch) and 169-170 (Clear branch) with explicit calls to both per-pin macros — `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set(); VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set();` and the matching Clear pair. The MCC comment in the function ("name it to 'VBUS_AH'") acknowledges the single-pin assumption.
114	
115	  6. **`initialization.c` `SYS_Initialize` — peripheral init order.** The USB-host MCC regen (2026-05-20) reordered SYS_Initialize so that `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize` run *before* `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize`. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.
116	
117	  7. **`usb_host_cdc.c` — accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0` in CDC ACM Communications-interface match.** Two checks (single-interface path ~line 677, IAD path ~line 798) currently require `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG-style USB-to-UART bridges (the on-board PIC/AVR debugger CDC, common across Microchip dev boards — including the fretboard board this project uses) declare the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol = USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC` (`0x00`). Without this patch the host CDC driver accepts the IAD via the TPL match (TPL ignores subclass/protocol) but rejects the comm interface inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign`, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to `STATE_ERROR`, and the app-level attach handler never fires. Patch: extend each check to `(... == AT_V250 || ... == NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. Two one-line OR additions. Re-apply after every USB-host MCC regen.
118	
119	  8. **`FreeRTOSConfig.h` — `portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS` / `portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE` macros + 64-bit counter type.** With `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS = 1` (set via `FREERTOS_GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` MCC symbol), FreeRTOS expects the application to provide a free-running counter. MCC's FreeRTOS Harmony component does not expose a knob for an app-specific counter source. Append at the end of `FreeRTOSConfig.h` (just before `#endif`):
120	     ```c
121	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
122	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
123	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
124	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
125	     ```
126	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.
127	
128	  9. **`drv_usb_udphs_device.c` — multi-IRP DMA arming in completion ISRs.** Stock UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch (line 1604+); IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in (line 2273-2284 of patched file via `iterator->next = irp_t`) but never get armed for transmission. `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after firing the callback but does not re-program DMA hardware. Result: only one IRP per "queue idle" sequence ever transmits — the rest sit `STATUS_PENDING` forever.
129	
130	      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). Then add a call after the queue advance in **two** places:
131	
132	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
133	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
134	
135	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. Helper carries the same cache-clean and DMA-program shape as the inline original, including the `__DSB(); __ISB();` barriers and the `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr` for the IRP data buffer.
136	
137	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.
138	
139	  Previously listed but now resolved or moot:
140	  - ~~`plib_xlcdc.c` LVDSPLL multiplier~~ — MCC now emits the chosen `MUL/FRACR/DIVPMC` for our 50 Hz target once the XLCDC driver MCC config was set correctly. Manual override no longer needed.
141	  - ~~`plib_lvdsc.c` `LVDSC_CFGR.DEN_POL`~~ — Latest Harmony gfx library intentionally omits the DEN_POL field. File reverted to MCC default; not load-bearing.
142	
143	  Recovery plan: re-apply all nine (small, self-contained diffs). Long-term options are (a) file MCC bugs, (b) shim into our own files, (c) live with periodic re-application.
144	
145	- **`log_csi_status` was removed** (Phase 5 restructure — tc358743 no longer auto-enables stream). If we ever want to re-query TC358743 CSI_STATUS/CSI_ERR bits, re-add the helper. The register addresses and masks are still defined in the file.
146	
147	- **ISC_Capture framebuffer sized for max 1920×1080 × 2 (~16 MB)** — wastes DDR at our current 720×480 use, but trivial at 256 MB total DDR and gives headroom for different sources. Reconsider if DDR becomes tight later.
148	
149	- **Retry semantics on source loss.** `app_coordinate_capture` uses a `capture_attempted` flag to prevent retry spam. On unlock it resets, so the next lock triggers a fresh Configure+Start. Untested for fast lock/unlock cycles — if the Wii toggles power, watch for state-machine glitches.
150	
151	- **Frame counter wraps at UINT32_MAX.** `g_frame_count` is 32-bit; at 60 fps it wraps after ~2.3 years continuous run. Not an immediate issue.
152	
153	- **`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS` likely needs to vary by difficulty.** 220 ms tuned well on Expert (notes are dense, the delay lines up against fast-moving notes near the strike line). Easy/Medium/Hard place notes higher up the highway with longer travel time, so the same 220 ms may strike too early. Open: per-difficulty preset, runtime-tunable from the manual-control surface, or auto-tuned from observed note-velocity. Defer until the game-state controller (spec §4.8) lands and difficulty is known to marvin — until then, expert-tuned 220 ms is the working default.

193	### 2026-06-01 — perf-log v3 plan: pivot to tuning visibility
194	
195	The low-level perf-log channel work is done (v1 framing/integrity, v2 STRIP + TASK_RUNTIME, multi-IRP throughput at 2.77 MB/s with zero drops). The wire's job pivots: from "prove bytes survived and the pipeline isn't dropping" to "show the host what the detection algorithm and actuator are thinking." Integrity records (SESSION, DROP, framing layer) keep their existing semantics — the trust they buy is load-bearing for everything else on the wire. Tuning records expand.
196	
197	One schema bump (v2 → v3) bundles four additions to avoid multiple rounds of firmware/host sync.
198	
199	**`DETECTOR_CONFIG` (new, low-rate / on-change).** Carries cv_marvin_v1 per-fret configuration the host needs to interpret the per-frame DETECTOR record:
200	- sample coords `(hx, hy, ex, ey)` per fret
201	- `hold_thresh`, `hold_release_frac`, `edge_thresh`
202	- color filter `target[3]`, `reject[3]` per fret
203	
204	Static today (compile-time tables in [`cv_marvin_v1.c`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c)); will become tunable when M6 calibration UI lands. Strip-relative pixel coords are computed host-side: `sample_x_in_strip = hx − strip.x`, since STRIP records already carry `(x, y, w, h)` in frame space.
205	
206	**`ACTUATOR` (new, per-publish or 1 Hz heartbeat).** Replaces the partial picture from `FBL_SEND` STAMP + `TIMING.publish_mask`:
207	- `intended_mask` — what the active producer wants
208	- `asserted_mask` — what's currently on the wire
209	- `strum_dir` — next direction (toggles each strum)
210	- `producer_id` — 1 byte tag (`timing_pipeline`, `manual_control`, future `game_state_controller`). The arbitration signal that's invisible today: when manual_control takes the wire, nothing on the wire indicates the handoff.
211	- ack timing fields — relate ACTUATOR ts to last `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` for transport-side latency.
212	
213	**`TIMING` (extended, per-frame snapshot).** Today's record carries counts only (`chord_window_fill`, `fifo_depth`). v3 carries the snapshot needed to answer "why did it publish *that* mask":
214	- `now_ms` (pipeline clock, anchors all `*_at_ms` deltas)
215	- `chord_open`, `chord_age_ms`, `chord_mask` — open window's accumulating mask
216	- `note_q_count`, `note_head_at_ms`, `note_head_mask`, `note_tail_mask` — front of queue + union of remainder
217	- `strum_q_count`, `strum_head_at_ms`, `strum_head_mask`, `strum_dir_next`
218	- `frets_active`, `strum_active`, `strum_release_at_ms`
219	- `release_pending_mask`, `release_min_at_ms`
220	- `publish_mask` (kept)
221	
222	~36 B body, per-detector-frame rate (60 Hz) ≈ 2 KB/s. Snapshot, not causal trace; if push/pop trace becomes necessary later, a sibling `TIMING_EVENT` record plugs in cleanly without revisiting this design.
223	
224	**CPU accounting completion.** TASK_RUNTIME already supports per-window CPU% (host subtracts adjacent `run_time_counter` records — wrap-safe modular subtraction; uint32 wire field is fine since 1-second window delta at 266 MHz is ~266M counts, well under 2³²). Three additions:
225	- `PERF_TASK_IDLE` — register `xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle()` so absolute CPU% = `1 − idle_delta / Σ_all_delta` is computable.
226	- **MCC per-task slots** (`LEGATO`, `XLCDC`, `MAXTOUCH`, `SYS_INPUT`, `USB_DEVICE`, `USB_HOST`, `DRV_USB_UDPHS`, `DRV_USB_HOST`, `APP`) — registered by string name via `xTaskGetHandle` from the perf-drain task at startup (pcName matches MCC's emitted `tasks.c` literals). MCC tasks are created in `SYS_Tasks()` just before `vTaskStartScheduler`, so handle lookup must happen *after* scheduler start — drain task does it on first iteration. Missing names log a warning and fall through into OTHER. Legato is the primary tuning target (Composer + Legato render path is the biggest single MCC CPU consumer); the rest come along essentially for free.
227	- `PERF_TASK_OTHER` — pseudo-slot that emits `Σ all-task runtime − Σ registered-task runtime` from `uxTaskGetSystemState`. With every notable named task registered, OTHER should normally idle near zero — a non-trivial OTHER means a task is active that we aren't naming yet (e.g. an unanticipated Harmony service).
228	
229	**Host-side pickups (marvin-perf).** [`web/api.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/api.py)'s `/capture/{id}/rtos` endpoint currently returns `cpu_pct: None  # Phase 2` and `cpu_pct_idle: None  # Phase 2`. With idle + OTHER on the wire, the per-window math fills those in. Viewer also gets:
230	- Strip overlays — sample dots in fret colors at `(hx,hy)` / `(ex,ey)` from DETECTOR_CONFIG, per-frame value labels from DETECTOR's `hold_dist` / `edge_dist`, threshold reference lines.
231	- Actuator panel — intended vs asserted mask, producer name, strum_dir history.
232	- Timing detail panel — chord window mask, note/strum queue head with deadlines, release-pending visualization.
233	
234	**What stays.** Framing layer (SOF + LEN + Fletcher-16), `SESSION`, `DROP`, `STAMP`, `STRIP`, `DETECTOR`, `TASK_HIGHWATER` all unchanged.
235	
236	**Out of scope this round.** Causal-trace `TIMING_EVENT` records, per-task MCC breakdown, ISR latency histograms, Cortex-A5 PMU instrumentation (cycles / cache misses / instructions retired), free-heap reporting (heap_1 is static post-init; Legato pool needs separate APIs).
