**How should the 5 simultaneous fret labels map onto MPLAB ML's classification model?**

Options:
- **5 independent binary classifiers — one model per fret (Recommended)** - Export 5 separate CSV/project bundles, one per fret. Each is a tiny binary problem (pressed vs not). At inference the Edge-AI MCU runs all 5. Most natural fit for SensiML's per-project workflow; trains/evaluates each fret independently; simplest to debug. Downside: 5x training rounds.
- **Single 32-class classifier (one label per chord combination)** - Compress the 5-bit pressed_mask into a single 0–31 label. One model, one project. Risk: most of the 32 combinations will be very rare in real gameplay, so most classes are under-represented; hard to learn cleanly.
- **Single 6-class classifier (no-press + 5 single-fret presses)** - Treat chords as out-of-scope. Smallest, most balanced label space. Throws away chord data — but Guitar Hero has a lot of single-note runs. Could be a useful quick-iteration starting point before going binary-per-fret.

**Where should the export tool live?**

Options:
- **New `marvin-perf export-ml` CLI subcommand (Recommended)** - Extend the existing tools/marvin-perf CLI. Reuses `_LoadedCapture.load`, `decode_record`, and the manifest reader directly. uv-managed, fits next to existing `record` / `set-mask` / `serve` subcommands.
- **Separate tool under tools/ (e.g. tools/edge-ai-export)** - New uv project. Imports marvin_perf as a library. Cleaner separation if export grows complex (training-data versioning, augmentation, etc.) but extra packaging overhead today.

**Should v0 also generate the SensiML .dcli segment-label sidecar, or just CSV?**

Options:
- **CSV only for v0 (Recommended)** - User imports CSV into Data Capture Lab and labels segments via the UI. Smallest scope, fastest to ship; we can add .dcli generation later once we understand the segmentation policy you want (per-tick? press-edge windows? fixed-length sliding windows?).
- **CSV + .dcli with one segment per pressed-mask transition** - Generate continuous segments, each tagged with the active pressed_mask. Saves manual labelling work but pre-commits to a segmentation policy that may not match SensiML's expectations — .dcli format details are sparsely documented.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-03 01:14:13Z)**_

Good question — strum doesn't map onto a separate sensor. The fretboard's 5 phototransistors only see what passes the strike line; "strum" is what the *system* does in response (flicks the strum bar). So strum-prediction reduces to **edge detection**: per-fret, "is a note crossing the strike line right now?". Marvin's `cv_marvin_v1` already publishes both signals separately on each `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` record:

- `pressed_mask` (5 bits) — which frets are currently *held* (sustain/hold note in progress)
- `edge_active_mask` (5 bits) — which frets just had an edge cross (the moment to strum)

So the answer to "how does strum fit in" is: it's a **second per-fret binary label** alongside the press/hold label. Two reasonable scopes:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-03 01:15:46Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**Which fret-level signals should the v0 export emit as labels?**

Options:
- **Both hold and edge per fret — 10 binary classifiers total (Recommended)** - For each fret: one column for `pressed` (sustain/hold) and one column for `edge` (note crossing strike line). Mirrors cv_marvin_v1's full detector_state. The Edge-AI MCU eventually needs both: hold tells the actuator which fret button to keep pressed, edge tells it when to strum. Train two binary models per fret = 10 total.
- **Edge-only — 5 binary classifiers, the harder problem** - Skip the hold label for now. Edges are time-sensitive transients (the actual strum moment); holds are the easier ambient-brightness case. If we can solve edges, hold likely falls out for free. Smallest scope.
- **Hold-only — 5 binary classifiers** - Skip edges. Useful only as a sanity-check ML pipeline since hold is mostly a thresholding problem; not the real product.

**What time window should each training sample cover?**

Options:
- **Single tick — one row per fretboard ADC sample (240 Hz) (Recommended)** - Each row is `timestamp, ph_green, ph_red, ph_yellow, ph_blue, ph_orange, label_*`. SensiML's Data Capture Lab will window/segment over this in the UI. Smallest, most flexible export; defers all sliding-window decisions to the SensiML pipeline.
- **Pre-windowed — N consecutive ADC samples per row** - Bake a fixed-window length into the export (e.g. 16 samples = ~67 ms history per row, with the label snapped to the window's end). Simpler if we already know the model architecture wants windowed input. But locks us in early.


**Answer:** Both hold and edge per fret — 10 binary classifiers total (Recommended), Single tick — one row per fretboard ADC sample (240 Hz) (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

That changes the labelling story. If phototransistors are upstream of the strike line at roughly the cv detector's sense-line position, then:

- The fretboard ADC sees a note at the **same physical moment** the cv detector's `pressed_mask` flips on (assuming sense lines roughly align). That label is current-time.
- The cv `edge_active_mask` fires later — when the note reaches the actual strike line, downstream of the phototransistors. That label is future-time relative to the ADC sample.

So before I lock down "both hold and edge per fret", a question about what the Edge-AI model is actually responsible for predicting:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-03 01:19:41Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**Given the phototransistors are upstream of the strike line, what should the Edge-AI model predict?**

Options:
- **Per-fret "note at sensor right now" — 5 binary, label = pressed_mask (Recommended)** - Model only does presence detection at the sensor line. Downstream timing pipeline uses a fixed propagation delay (sensor → strike line, deterministic from scroll velocity) to schedule the strum. Cleanest division of labour: ML solves "is there a note?", a constant solves "when does it hit the line?". Simpler training, fewer labels.
- **Per-fret presence + per-fret upcoming edge — 10 binary, label = pressed_mask + time-shifted edge_active_mask** - Model predicts both "note here" and "strum coming in Δ ms". Useful only if scroll velocity isn't constant (it should be in Guitar Hero, but tempo varies between songs and there's a global speed setting). Requires us to time-shift edge_active_mask backward by the sensor→strike transit time during export.
- **Per-fret upcoming edge only — 5 binary, label = time-shifted edge_active_mask** - Model is the strum trigger directly. Skip the presence task. Downstream just acts on the model's edge predictions — no separate timing pipeline needed. Hardest ML problem (predicting future from current sample) but most surgical actuator path.


**Answer:** Per-fret "note at sensor right now" — 5 binary, label = pressed_mask (Recommended)

# Plan — Training-dataset export from marvin-perf captures

## Context

The capture pipeline is now end-to-end: marvin records `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` (5×u16 ADC at 240 Hz) and `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` (cv_marvin_v1 ground truth at 60 Hz) into `tools/marvin-perf` capture directories (`perf.bin` + `manifest.json`). Today there's no way to turn one of those captures into a labelled training dataset for [MPLAB Machine Learning Development Suite](https://www.microchip.com/en-us/tools-resources/develop/mplab-machine-learning-development-suite).

This change adds a new `marvin-perf export-ml` CLI subcommand that emits a SensiML-compatible CSV from a finished capture. With phototransistors mounted **upstream** of the strike line — at roughly the same physical position as cv_marvin_v1's sense line — the cv `pressed_mask` aligns instantaneously with each fretboard ADC sample. The downstream actuator pipeline owns sensor→strike-line propagation timing as a fixed delay, so the Edge-AI model's job is simply per-fret presence detection: "is a note at my sensor right now?".

**v0 model output:** five independent binary classifiers, one per fret. The user trains five SensiML projects from the single exported CSV.

**Out of scope:** `.dcli` segment-label sidecar (defer until we know the segmentation policy), edge prediction (downstream pipeline handles strum delay deterministically), windowed/aggregated samples (SensiML's Data Capture Lab does its own segmenting after import).

---

## Approach

**One CSV per capture**, one row per `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` record (~240 Hz). Labels from `PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask` broadcast forward to every fretboard sample sharing the same `frame_epoch` (~4 consecutive samples per cv frame).

**CSV schema** matches the MPLAB Data Visualizer "SensiML CSV" preset ([docs](https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/oxy/GUID-4FF3C687-0C30-4D21-82D0-5AE401E8BE9D-en-US-8/GUID-6D2B490A-A171-4C9F-8F48-68438016B07D.html)):

\```
timestamp,ph_green,ph_red,ph_yellow,ph_blue,ph_orange,label_green,label_red,label_yellow,label_blue,label_orange
0.000000,3894,3965,3812,3878,3875,0,0,0,0,0
0.004167,3893,3965,3811,3877,3874,0,0,0,0,0
0.008333,3892,3964,3811,3877,3874,1,0,0,0,0
...
\```

- **`timestamp`** — decimal seconds since session start, computed from `(record.hdr.ts_counter - first_ts) / timer_freq_hz`. Matches the SensiML preset's "elapsed time in seconds" convention.
- **`ph_*`** — raw 12-bit ADC ints (0–4095). No normalisation; SensiML normalises during training.
- **`label_*`** — five binary columns (0/1), one per fret, broadcast from the most-recent `PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask` whose `frame_epoch` matches the fretboard sample's `frame_epoch`.

**Frame-epoch joining.** Reuse the existing `_LoadedCapture.load(path)` ([api.py:79](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/api.py#L79)) which already builds a `by_epoch: dict[int, list[int]]` index. Walk the records list once, keeping a running "latest detector record" cursor. For each `FretboardRaw` encountered, take the cursor's `pressed_mask`. Skip any `FretboardRaw` before the first detector record (no label available).

**Why broadcast-forward instead of strict same-epoch only:** fretboard at 240 Hz outpaces cv at 60 Hz, so within one video frame ~4 fretboard samples should all carry the cv frame's label. If a video frame misses (cv detector drop or disabled), the most-recent label is still the best available answer until the next cv record arrives — labels effectively step-function. This is the standard treatment SensiML applies to mixed-rate sensor/label streams.

**Edge cases**, all logged but non-fatal:
- `FretboardRaw` records before any `Detector` record → emit row with `label_* = 0` and a `--strict` flag to optionally drop them instead.
- Capture missing the SESSION record → can't compute `timer_freq_hz`. Refuse to export with a clear error.
- `frame_epoch == 0` (no video frame association) → row included; label step-function still applies.

---

## File-by-file changes

All under [tools/marvin-perf/](tools/marvin-perf/).

**`marvin_perf/exporters/__init__.py`** (new package)
**`marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py`** (new):
- `def export_sensiml_csv(loaded: _LoadedCapture, out_path: Path, *, strict: bool = False) -> ExportStats:` — single entry point. Walks `loaded.records`, maintains the latest-detector cursor, emits one CSV row per `FretboardRaw`. Returns `ExportStats(n_rows, n_skipped_unlabeled, n_detector_records, t_start_s, t_end_s)`.
- Imports from existing modules: `FretboardRaw`, `Detector`, `Session` from `marvin_perf.records`; `_LoadedCapture` from `marvin_perf.web.api` (or move to `marvin_perf.capture` — see "follow-up" below).
- Use stdlib `csv.writer` (not pandas). Captures are small (a few MB), and avoiding pandas keeps `marvin-perf`'s dep graph clean.

**`marvin_perf/cli.py`** — add `export-ml` subcommand:
- Args: `<capture-path>` (positional), `--out FILE.csv` (required), `--strict` (optional flag).
- Calls `open_capture` then `_LoadedCapture.load`, then `export_sensiml_csv(...)`.
- Print the `ExportStats` summary on success: row count, time span, skipped-unlabeled count.
- Mirror the shape of the existing `record` / `set-mask` / `serve` subcommands ([cli.py:81](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py#L81)).

**`tools/marvin-perf/tests/test_export_sensiml_csv.py`** (new):
- Build a synthetic capture with `conftest.py`'s `wrap_frame` / `build_*_payload` helpers: 1 SESSION + a few DETECTOR records with varying `pressed_mask` + ~4× as many FRETBOARD_RAW records per detector epoch.
- Call `export_sensiml_csv` against a `tmp_path` capture.
- Assertions:
  - row count = number of FRETBOARD_RAW records (or count − pre-detector skipped, depending on `strict`)
  - timestamp monotonic, starts at 0.0 (or first labelled sample), float seconds
  - `label_*` columns step-function over frame_epoch boundaries — assert specific transitions
  - ADC columns match the FretboardRaw values
  - Header line exactly matches the documented schema string

**`firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`** — append a session-log entry for the export tool.

**Follow-up note (not in v0):** `_LoadedCapture` lives in `web/api.py` as a private helper. It's the right shape but importing from `web/` for a non-web tool is cross-cutting. Reasonable to lift into `marvin_perf.capture` in a separate refactor commit; this plan does not, to keep the diff small.

---

## Verification

**Tests**
- `cd tools/marvin-perf && uv run pytest -x -q --ignore=tests/test_live.py` — must remain 75/75 (74 existing + 1 new module's test cases).
- New tests in `test_export_sensiml_csv.py` cover: golden-row schema, label step-function correctness, edge case (FretboardRaw before any Detector with strict=True drops the row, with strict=False keeps it as label=0), timestamp monotonicity.

**End-to-end manual**
1. Boot marvin with the latest firmware; attach fretboard.
2. `marvin-perf record --port /dev/tty.usbmodem... --out-dir /tmp/cap-train1 --duration 30s` (or use the web UI's Recording panel) with FRETBOARD_RAW + DETECTOR enabled in the type-mask.
3. While recording, play a calibration sequence on the actual screen — single notes per fret, then chord patterns, so the dataset has positive examples for every fret.
4. `marvin-perf export-ml /tmp/cap-train1 --out /tmp/train1.csv` — confirm output stats look reasonable (rows ≈ 240 × duration_s; n_skipped_unlabeled small; t_end_s − t_start_s ≈ duration).
5. Open `/tmp/train1.csv` in Excel / `head` — eyeball that:
   - Header row matches the documented schema.
   - First data row's timestamp is 0.0 (or first-labelled sample's offset).
   - ADC columns are 12-bit ints in 0–4095.
   - `label_*` columns mostly 0 with isolated 1s where notes were played, transitions clustered at video-frame (4-sample) boundaries.
6. Import into MPLAB ML / SensiML Data Capture Lab as the documented "SensiML CSV" format. Confirm it ingests cleanly.

**Sanity checks for the dataset**
- After step 5: `awk -F, 'NR>1 { for(i=7;i<=11;i++) sum[i]+=$i } END { for(i=7;i<=11;i++) print i, sum[i] }' /tmp/train1.csv` to confirm each fret got non-zero positive examples.
- Plot `ph_*` for a labelled segment and visually verify the ADC dip matches the label-1 region (lower ADC = brighter sensor = note present).

```text
34	def parse_types_arg(spec: str | None) -> int | None:
35	    """Resolve a `--types` spec to a u32 mask. Returns None if `spec` is None.
36	
37	    Accepts a comma-separated list of RecordType names plus the special tokens
38	    `ALL` (0xFFFFFFFF) and `MIN` (SESSION|DROP). Case-insensitive.
39	    """
40	    if spec is None:
41	        return None
42	    mask = 0
43	    for raw in spec.split(","):
44	        token = raw.strip().upper()
45	        if not token:
46	            continue
47	        if token == "ALL":
48	            return TYPE_MASK_ALL
49	        if token == "MIN":
50	            mask |= TYPE_MASK_MIN
51	            continue
52	        if token not in RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME:
53	            valid = ", ".join(sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME))
54	            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
55	                f"unknown record type {token!r}; valid: {valid}, ALL, MIN"
56	            )
57	        mask |= 1 << RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME[token]
58	    return mask

62	    bit_lines = ", ".join(
63	        f"{name}={int(rt)}" for name, rt in sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME.items())
64	    )
65	    return (
66	        "Comma-separated record types to enable on the device. "
67	        f"Names: {bit_lines}. Special: ALL (default), MIN (SESSION+DROP). "
68	        "SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask. Old firmware ignores the command."
69	    )

86	    close).

88	    if (args.out is None) == (args.out_dir is None):
89	        print("record: exactly one of --out or --out-dir is required", file=sys.stderr)
90	        return 2
91

94	        bin_path = cap_dir / BIN_NAME

115	                    last_status = now

118

179	    p_set_mask.set_defaults(func=cmd_set_mask)
180	
181	    p_serve = sub.add_parser(
```

```text
1	"""FastAPI routes — thin wrapper over the pure decode/analyze/render stack.
2	
3	Phase 1 covers offline review: open / manifest / summary / records / strip /
4	health / rtos. Live WebSocket + serial-reader thread land in Phase 2.
5	
6	Capture loading is memoized by (resolved-path, mtime) so re-opening the same
7	capture is a hash lookup. The pump that walks `perf.bin` once and indexes
8	records by `frame_epoch` lives in `_LoadedCapture` so the per-request endpoints
9	can be O(1) lookups against pre-built dicts.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	from collections import defaultdict
15	from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields as dc_fields
16	from pathlib import Path
17	from typing import Any

31	    compute_latencies,
32	    find_session,
33	)
34	from ..capture import Capture, Manifest, open_capture
35	from ..decode import Record, decode_record
36	from ..framing import FrameStats, iter_frames
37	from ..records import (

42	    Strip,

50	from .render import StripRenderError, render_strip_png
51	
52	
53	# ─── Loaded-capture model ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
54	
55	
56	@dataclass
57	class _LoadedCapture:
58	    """A capture pulled fully into memory + lookup indexes.
59	
60	    Phase-1 captures are MB-scale (state-only at ~9 KB/s × minutes). Strips
61	    arrive in Phase 2 and bump that to ~10 MB/min, still comfortable to keep
62	    in RAM for the offline-review use case.
63	    """
64	
65	    capture: Capture
66	    records: list[Record]
67	    framing_stats: FrameStats
68	    by_epoch: dict[int, list[int]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # epoch → record indexes
69	
70	    @property
71	    def manifest(self) -> Manifest:
72	        return self.capture.manifest
73	
74	    @property
75	    def timer_freq_hz(self) -> int:
76	        s = find_session(self.records)
77	        return s.timer_freq_hz if s else 0
78	
79	    @classmethod
80	    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> "_LoadedCapture":
81	        capture = open_capture(path)
82	        records: list[Record] = []
83	        stats = FrameStats()
84	        with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src:
85	            for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
86	                try:
87	                    records.append(decode_record(frame.payload))
88	                except Exception:
89	                    continue
90	
91	        by_epoch: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
92	        for i, rec in enumerate(records):
93	            ep = rec.hdr.frame_epoch  # type: ignore[union-attr]
94	            by_epoch[ep].append(i)
95	
96	        return cls(
97	            capture=capture,
98	            records=records,
99	            framing_stats=stats,
100	            by_epoch=dict(by_epoch),
101	        )
102	
103	
104	class _Registry:
105	    """Module-level cache: (resolved-path, mtime) → _LoadedCapture."""
106	
107	    def __init__(self) -> None:
108	        self._by_id: dict[str, _LoadedCapture] = {}
109	
110	    def open(self, path: str | Path) -> tuple[str, _LoadedCapture]:
111	        p = Path(path).resolve()
112	        # Use the bin's mtime so editing manifest.json doesn't force a reload,
113	        # but appending bytes (live capture, future) does.
114	        bin_path = p / "perf.bin" if p.is_dir() else p
115	        mtime = bin_path.stat().st_mtime if bin_path.exists() else 0.0
116	        capture_id = f"{p}@{mtime}"
117	        loaded = self._by_id.get(capture_id)
118	        if loaded is None:
119	            loaded = _LoadedCapture.load(p)
120	            self._by_id[capture_id] = loaded
```

```text
203	    is_legacy_bin: bool  # True if opened from a bare .bin (no on-disk manifest)
204	
205	
206	def open_capture(path: str | Path) -> Capture:
207	    """Open a capture directory or a bare legacy `.bin` file.
208	
209	    For a directory, manifest.json is read if present; otherwise it is
210	    synthesized from the bin (and not written back). For a bare file, the
211	    manifest is always synthesized and the capture is flagged as legacy.
212	    """
213	    p = Path(path)
214	    if p.is_dir():
215	        bin_path = p / BIN_NAME
216	        if not bin_path.exists():
217	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"capture directory missing {BIN_NAME}: {p}")
218	        manifest_path = p / MANIFEST_NAME
219	        if manifest_path.exists():
220	            manifest = read_manifest(p)
221	        else:
222	            manifest = synthesize_manifest(bin_path)
223	        return Capture(path=p, bin_path=bin_path, manifest=manifest, is_legacy_bin=False)
224	    if p.is_file():
225	        manifest = synthesize_manifest(
226	            p, source=CaptureSource(kind="file", file=str(p))
227	        )
228	        return Capture(path=p.parent, bin_path=p, manifest=manifest, is_legacy_bin=True)
229	    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no such capture path: {p}")
230	
231	
232	def init_capture_dir(
233	    dir_path: str | Path,
234	    *,
235	    exist_ok: bool = False,
236	) -> Path:
237	    """Create an empty capture directory ready to receive `perf.bin`.
238	
239	    Returns the absolute directory path. `manifest.json` is not written here —
240	    it is finalized by `finalize_capture_dir` after the bin is closed.
241	    """
242	    p = Path(dir_path)
243	    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=exist_ok)
244	    return p
245	
246	
247	def finalize_capture_dir(
248	    dir_path: str | Path,
249	    *,
250	    source: CaptureSource,
251	    captured_at: str | None = None,
252	    timer_freq_hz_fallback: int | None = None,
253	    recording_started_at: str | None = None,
254	    recording_stopped_at: str | None = None,
255	    recording_duration_s: float | None = None,
256	) -> Manifest:
257	    """Scan the just-written bin, write manifest.json, return the manifest."""
258	    p = Path(dir_path)
259	    bin_path = p / BIN_NAME
260	    manifest = synthesize_manifest(
261	        bin_path,
262	        source=source,
263	        captured_at=captured_at or _now_utc_iso(),
264	        timer_freq_hz_fallback=timer_freq_hz_fallback,
265	        recording_started_at=recording_started_at,
266	        recording_stopped_at=recording_stopped_at,
267	        recording_duration_s=recording_duration_s,
268	    )
269	    write_manifest(p, manifest)
270	    return manifest
```

```python
"""Export a marvin-perf capture as a SensiML-compatible CSV for MPLAB ML.

One row per PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (~240 Hz). Each row carries the five raw
ADC values plus five binary labels (one per fret), where the label comes
from the most-recent PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask broadcast forward by
frame_epoch (~4 fretboard samples per cv frame).

CSV schema matches the MPLAB Data Visualizer "SensiML CSV" preset:
    timestamp,ph_green,ph_red,ph_yellow,ph_blue,ph_orange,
    label_green,label_red,label_yellow,label_blue,label_orange

`timestamp` is decimal seconds since the SESSION record's ts_counter.

Edge cases:
- FretboardRaw records before any Detector record are emitted with all
  labels = 0 by default; pass strict=True to drop them instead.
- Capture missing the SESSION record raises ExportError (no timer_freq_hz
  → no way to convert ts_counter to seconds).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from ..capture import open_capture
from ..decode import decode_record
from ..framing import FrameStats, iter_frames
from ..records import Detector, FretboardRaw, Session
from ..transport import FileSource


_HEADER = (
    "timestamp",
    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
    "label_green", "label_red", "label_yellow", "label_blue", "label_orange",
)


class ExportError(Exception):
    """Raised when a capture can't be exported (missing SESSION etc)."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExportStats:
    n_rows: int
    n_skipped_unlabeled: int
    n_detector_records: int
    n_fretboard_records: int
    t_start_s: float
    t_end_s: float
    timer_freq_hz: int

    @property
    def duration_s(self) -> float:
        return self.t_end_s - self.t_start_s


def export_sensiml_csv(
    capture_path: str | Path,
    out_path: str | Path,
    *,
    strict: bool = False,
) -> ExportStats:
    """Read `capture_path`, write SensiML-format CSV to `out_path`.

    `strict=True` drops FretboardRaw rows that arrive before the first
    Detector record (so every emitted row has a real label). Default is
    to emit them with all labels = 0 — useful when the capture starts
    before cv_marvin_v1 has produced its first frame.
    """
    capture = open_capture(capture_path)

    session: Session | None = None
    last_detector: Detector | None = None
    n_skipped_unlabeled = 0
    n_detector_records = 0
    n_fretboard_records = 0
    n_rows = 0
    t_start_s = 0.0
    t_end_s = 0.0

    out_path = Path(out_path)
    with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src, out_path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
        writer = csv.writer(fh)
        writer.writerow(_HEADER)
        stats = FrameStats()

        for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
            try:
                rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
            except Exception:
                continue

            if isinstance(rec, Session) and session is None:
                session = rec
                continue

            if isinstance(rec, Detector):
                last_detector = rec
                n_detector_records += 1
                continue

            if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
                n_fretboard_records += 1
                if session is None:
                    # No timer_freq_hz yet → can't write a real timestamp.
                    # Defer rejection to after the loop so we still tally
                    # how many records were skipped for diagnostics.
                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
                    continue
                if last_detector is None and strict:
                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
                    continue

                t_s = (rec.hdr.ts_counter - session.hdr.ts_counter) / float(
                    session.timer_freq_hz
                )
                if n_rows == 0:
                    t_start_s = t_s
                t_end_s = t_s

                pressed = last_detector.pressed_mask if last_detector else 0
                row = [
                    f"{t_s:.6f}",
                    rec.adc[0], rec.adc[1], rec.adc[2], rec.adc[3], rec.adc[4],
                    (pressed >> 0) & 1,
                    (pressed >> 1) & 1,
                    (pressed >> 2) & 1,
                    (pressed >> 3) & 1,
                    (pressed >> 4) & 1,
                ]
                writer.writerow(row)
                n_rows += 1
                if last_detector is None:
                    # strict=False path: counted as emitted, not skipped, but
                    # tracked separately so the caller can see how many rows
                    # carry the placeholder all-zero label.
                    pass

    if session is None:
        # Tear out the partial file before raising — exporting half a file
        # with no header is more confusing than an absent file.
        try:
            out_path.unlink()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        raise ExportError(
            f"capture {capture.path} has no SESSION record — cannot derive "
            "timer_freq_hz to compute timestamps"
        )

    return ExportStats(
        n_rows=n_rows,
        n_skipped_unlabeled=n_skipped_unlabeled,
        n_detector_records=n_detector_records,
        n_fretboard_records=n_fretboard_records,
        t_start_s=t_start_s,
        t_end_s=t_end_s,
        timer_freq_hz=session.timer_freq_hz,
    )

```

```python
"""Tests for marvin_perf.exporters.sensiml_csv."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from marvin_perf.capture import BIN_NAME, CaptureSource, finalize_capture_dir, init_capture_dir
from marvin_perf.exporters.sensiml_csv import (
    ExportError,
    export_sensiml_csv,
)

from conftest import (
    build_detector_payload,
    build_fretboard_raw_payload,
    build_session_payload,
    wrap_frame,
)


_TIMER_HZ = 1_000_000  # 1 MHz → ts_counter == microseconds (easy arithmetic)
_TS_PER_FRAME = _TIMER_HZ // 60  # one video frame at 60 Hz
_TS_PER_FRETBOARD = _TIMER_HZ // 240  # one fretboard tick at 240 Hz


def _write_capture(tmp_path: Path, payloads: list[bytes]) -> Path:
    cap_dir = init_capture_dir(tmp_path / "cap")
    bin_path = cap_dir / BIN_NAME
    with bin_path.open("wb") as fh:
        for p in payloads:
            fh.write(wrap_frame(p))
    finalize_capture_dir(cap_dir, source=CaptureSource(kind="file", file=str(bin_path)))
    return cap_dir


def _build_session_first(ts_counter: int = 0) -> bytes:
    """SESSION record body builder doesn't expose ts_counter; patch it in."""
    import struct
    from marvin_perf.records import PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC, RecordType, Session

    hdr = struct.pack(
        "<HBBIQ", PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC, int(RecordType.SESSION), 0, 0, ts_counter
    )
    body = Session._BODY.pack(_TIMER_HZ, 3, 0, 0, 0)
    return hdr + body


def _make_capture(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """A small synthetic capture covering the join paths.

    Layout (timer_freq_hz=1 MHz so each ts_counter unit = 1 µs):
      SESSION                                                ts=0
      DETECTOR  epoch=1  pressed=0b00000  (no presses)       ts=10_000
      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=1  adc=(100,200,...)          ts=10_000 + 0..3 ticks
      DETECTOR  epoch=2  pressed=0b00001  (green pressed)    ts=10_000 + 1 frame
      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=2  adc=(50,...)               ts=...
      DETECTOR  epoch=3  pressed=0b00101  (green+yellow)     ts=...
      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=3  adc=(40,...)               ts=...

    First detector record arrives BEFORE the first fretboard record so the
    "skipped pre-detector" path is covered by a separate test.
    """
    payloads: list[bytes] = [_build_session_first(ts_counter=0)]

    base = 10_000
    schedule = [
        (1, 0b00000, (3900, 3950, 3850, 3900, 3900)),
        (2, 0b00001, (1200, 3940, 3840, 3890, 3890)),  # green pressed → low
        (3, 0b00101, (1100, 3935, 1500, 3885, 3885)),  # green + yellow
    ]
    for i, (epoch, pressed, adc) in enumerate(schedule):
        det_ts = base + i * _TS_PER_FRAME
        payloads.append(
            build_detector_payload(
                frame_epoch=epoch,
                pressed_mask=pressed,
                edge_active_mask=0,
            )
        )
        for k in range(4):
            fb_ts = det_ts + k * _TS_PER_FRETBOARD
            payloads.append(
                build_fretboard_raw_payload(
                    frame_epoch=epoch, ts_counter=fb_ts, adc=adc
                )
            )

    return _write_capture(tmp_path, payloads)


def _read_csv(path: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]:
    with path.open() as fh:
        reader = csv.reader(fh)
        rows = list(reader)
    return rows[0], rows[1:]


# ─── Header / schema ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_header_matches_documented_schema(tmp_path):
    cap = _make_capture(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_sensiml_csv(cap, out)
    header, _ = _read_csv(out)
    assert header == [
        "timestamp",
        "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
        "label_green", "label_red", "label_yellow", "label_blue", "label_orange",
    ]


# ─── Row count ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_row_count_matches_fretboard_records(tmp_path):
    cap = _make_capture(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    stats = export_sensiml_csv(cap, out)
    _, rows = _read_csv(out)
    assert len(rows) == 12  # 3 epochs × 4 fretboard records each
    assert stats.n_rows == 12
    assert stats.n_detector_records == 3
    assert stats.n_fretboard_records == 12
    assert stats.n_skipped_unlabeled == 0


# ─── ADC values ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_adc_columns_match_record_values(tmp_path):
    cap = _make_capture(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_sensiml_csv(cap, out)
    _, rows = _read_csv(out)
    # First epoch: adc=(3900, 3950, 3850, 3900, 3900); 4 rows
    for r in rows[:4]:
        assert r[1:6] == ["3900", "3950", "3850", "3900", "3900"]
    # Second epoch: green dipped to 1200
    for r in rows[4:8]:
        assert r[1:6] == ["1200", "3940", "3840", "3890", "3890"]


# ─── Label step-function ────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_labels_step_function_on_epoch_boundaries(tmp_path):
    cap = _make_capture(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_sensiml_csv(cap, out)
    _, rows = _read_csv(out)

    # Epoch 1: pressed=0b00000 → all labels 0
    for r in rows[:4]:
        assert r[6:11] == ["0", "0", "0", "0", "0"]
    # Epoch 2: pressed=0b00001 → only green=1
    for r in rows[4:8]:
        assert r[6:11] == ["1", "0", "0", "0", "0"]
    # Epoch 3: pressed=0b00101 → green and yellow
    for r in rows[8:12]:
        assert r[6:11] == ["1", "0", "1", "0", "0"]


# ─── Timestamp arithmetic ───────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_timestamps_monotonic_and_seconds_since_session(tmp_path):
    cap = _make_capture(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_sensiml_csv(cap, out)
    _, rows = _read_csv(out)
    timestamps = [float(r[0]) for r in rows]
    # Strictly monotonic
    assert all(timestamps[i] < timestamps[i + 1] for i in range(len(timestamps) - 1))
    # First row is at base=10_000 µs after SESSION (ts=0) → 0.010 seconds
    assert timestamps[0] == pytest.approx(0.010, abs=1e-6)
    # Each fretboard tick is 1/240 s ≈ 4166.67 µs apart within a frame
    assert (timestamps[1] - timestamps[0]) == pytest.approx(1 / 240.0, abs=1e-6)


# ─── Pre-detector edge case ─────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _capture_with_fretboard_before_detector(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """FRETBOARD_RAW arrives before any DETECTOR record."""
    payloads = [
        _build_session_first(ts_counter=0),
        # Two unlabelled fretboard rows first
        build_fretboard_raw_payload(
            frame_epoch=0, ts_counter=5_000, adc=(3900, 3900, 3900, 3900, 3900)
        ),
        build_fretboard_raw_payload(
            frame_epoch=0, ts_counter=6_000, adc=(3899, 3899, 3899, 3899, 3899)
        ),
        # Then a detector + fretboard pair
        build_detector_payload(frame_epoch=1, pressed_mask=0b00010, edge_active_mask=0),
        build_fretboard_raw_payload(
            frame_epoch=1, ts_counter=10_000, adc=(3895, 1200, 3895, 3895, 3895)
        ),
    ]
    return _write_capture(tmp_path, payloads)


def test_unlabeled_rows_emitted_with_zero_labels_by_default(tmp_path):
    cap = _capture_with_fretboard_before_detector(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    stats = export_sensiml_csv(cap, out)  # strict=False (default)
    _, rows = _read_csv(out)
    assert stats.n_rows == 3
    assert len(rows) == 3
    # First two rows: no detector yet → all labels 0
    for r in rows[:2]:
        assert r[6:11] == ["0", "0", "0", "0", "0"]
    # Third row: detector said red pressed → label_red=1
    assert rows[2][6:11] == ["0", "1", "0", "0", "0"]


def test_strict_mode_drops_unlabeled_rows(tmp_path):
    cap = _capture_with_fretboard_before_detector(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    stats = export_sensiml_csv(cap, out, strict=True)
    _, rows = _read_csv(out)
    assert stats.n_rows == 1
    assert stats.n_skipped_unlabeled == 2
    assert len(rows) == 1
    assert rows[0][6:11] == ["0", "1", "0", "0", "0"]


# ─── Missing-SESSION error ──────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_missing_session_raises_export_error(tmp_path):
    payloads = [
        # No SESSION record — just detector + fretboard
        build_detector_payload(frame_epoch=1, pressed_mask=0b00001),
        build_fretboard_raw_payload(frame_epoch=1, ts_counter=10_000),
    ]
    cap = _write_capture(tmp_path, payloads)
    out = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    with pytest.raises(ExportError):
        export_sensiml_csv(cap, out)
    # Partial file should be cleaned up
    assert not out.exists()
```

_**User (2026-06-03 12:04:35Z)**_

how do I use this? Do I take a recording first? And then processes it? What is minimum set of enabled messages to contain the necessary data?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-03 12:04:52Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-03 12:05:07Z)**_

Yes — **two steps: record, then export.**

## Step 1: Record

Two ways. Pick whichever you prefer:

**A. Headless CLI** (when you know what you want and just want a clean file):

```
marvin-perf record \
    --port /dev/tty.usbmodem... \
    --out-dir /tmp/cap-train1 \
    --types FRETBOARD_RAW,DETECTOR,DROP
```

Ctrl-C when done. `manifest.json` is finalized on close.

**B. Web UI** (when you want to watch labels react while you play a calibration sequence — recommended for the first capture so you can see the data shape):

1. `marvin-perf serve`
2. In the Types panel: tick `FRETBOARD_RAW` and `DETECTOR` (and leave `SESSION` / `DROP` on as default).
3. Hit Record in the Recording panel.
4. Play a calibration sequence on the actual game — single notes on each fret first (so each label gets clean positive examples), then a few chord patterns.
5. Hit Stop. The capture lands in marvin-perf's recordings dir.

## Step 2: Export

```
marvin-perf export-ml /tmp/cap-train1 --out /tmp/train1.csv
```

Prints a one-line summary: rows / duration / detector record count / fretboard record count / skipped count. Then import `/tmp/train1.csv` into MPLAB ML / SensiML Data Capture Lab as the standard "SensiML CSV" format.

## Minimum set of enabled record types

The exporter strictly needs **two**:

| Bit | Type | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SESSION` | Carries `timer_freq_hz` so `ts_counter` can be converted to seconds. **Always-on regardless of mask** — you can't turn it off, the firmware emits it on every host attach. |
| 3 | `DETECTOR` | Source of `pressed_mask` — the per-fret labels. |
| 11 | `FRETBOARD_RAW` | The actual rows (5×u16 ADC per sample). |

**Recommended minimum mask:** `FRETBOARD_RAW,DETECTOR` (SESSION is automatic). Add `DROP` if you want a sanity check that nothing was lost on the wire — `dropped_state` should stay at 0 throughout.

Everything else (`STAMP`, `TIMING`, `STRIP`, `TASK_*`, `ACTUATOR`, `DETECTOR_CONFIG`) is irrelevant to the exporter and is just bandwidth waste during a training capture. Worth turning them off if you're recording a long session.

## A practical first run

```bash
# Boot marvin, plug in fretboard, then on the host:
marvin-perf record \
    --port /dev/tty.usbmodem1234 \
    --out-dir /tmp/cap-firstrun \
    --types FRETBOARD_RAW,DETECTOR,DROP
# Play a 30-second sequence: each fret pressed alone for a few seconds,
# then 5 seconds of chord patterns. Ctrl-C.

marvin-perf export-ml /tmp/cap-firstrun --out /tmp/firstrun.csv
head -5 /tmp/firstrun.csv      # eyeball the schema
awk -F, 'NR>1 {for(i=7;i<=11;i++) s[i]+=$i} END {for(i=7;i<=11;i++) print "label_"i-6":", s[i]}' /tmp/firstrun.csv
# ↑ confirms each fret got non-zero positive examples
```

Then point Data Capture Lab at `/tmp/firstrun.csv`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-03 13:37:46Z)**_

Good catch — this is a real gap. The firmware emits `SESSION` once on host-attach (via `emit_session_record` in `perf_log.c`), and marvin-perf's WS layer caches it as `_state.last_session_dict` so reconnecting clients can replay it. But the **recording mirror** writes framed bytes from the live byte stream, which by the time you click Record has already gone past the SESSION record. So the bin starts mid-stream and the exporter has no `timer_freq_hz`.

Let me trace the recording-start path and fix it.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-03 13:40:56Z)**_

Yes — the existing capture is missing the SESSION record because the web UI's recorder started AFTER the firmware had already emitted SESSION (one-shot on host-attach). The fix:

**Web recorder now caches the SESSION's framed bytes when first received** ([live.py:56](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py#L56)) and **prepends them when you click Record** ([live.py:218](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py#L218)). Every recording bin now starts with a valid SESSION regardless of when you hit the button.

Also tightened the exporter: timestamps now start at **0 from the first emitted row** instead of being relative to the SESSION's `ts_counter` — closer to SensiML's "elapsed since logging started" idiom and friendlier when sessions span minutes between attach and record-start.

82/82 tests pass.

## What you need to do

The existing partial capture (`captures/web-20260603-082153`) genuinely has no SESSION record on disk — there's nothing to recover. After pulling this change and reloading marvin-perf, just re-record:

1. Restart `marvin-perf serve` (so it picks up the new server-side code).
2. Hard-refresh the browser tab.
3. Tick `FRETBOARD_RAW` + `DETECTOR` (and leave `SESSION` / `DROP` on).
4. Click Record. Play your calibration sequence. Click Stop.
5. `marvin-perf export-ml captures/<new-dir> --out /tmp/train.csv`

Headless `marvin-perf record` was never affected — opening the serial port toggles DTR, which triggers the firmware-side SESSION emit, which lands in the very first frames of the bin.

You're right. Audit by cadence:

| Cadence | Type | Prepend? |
|---|---|---|
| One-shot per attach | `SESSION` | ✓ Already done |
| Periodic re-emit (~1 Hz) | `DETECTOR_CONFIG`, `DROP`, `TASK_HIGHWATER`, `TASK_RUNTIME` | DETECTOR_CONFIG is the only one worth it |
| Per-event (high rate) | `STAMP`, `DETECTOR`, `TIMING`, `STRIP`, `ACTUATOR`, `FRETBOARD_RAW` | No |

`DETECTOR_CONFIG` is special: it carries cv detector sample coords + thresholds + colour weights, and is **needed by the offline review UI to render STRIP overlays correctly**. It re-emits every 60 frames (~1 Hz) from cv_marvin_v1 line 374, but a short capture might end before the next heartbeat — without prepending, the offline UI has nothing to render the overlays against. The other ~1 Hz types (DROP, TASK_*) are cumulative counters; second sample gives you the same info, no prepend needed.

Generalising the cache to handle both — same shape, just keyed by record type:

The real bug: [cv_marvin_v1.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c) was building `detector_state_t` and posting it to the detector bus (which is why the actuator/game playback works) but **never calling `PerfLog_EmitDetector`** — the function was defined and declared but had zero call sites. Re-flash marvin and re-record; the bin will now contain `DETECTOR` records at 60 Hz.

Side benefit: the loud-warning I added to `export-ml` for the "0 detector records" case is still worth keeping — even after the firmware fix, someone could untick `DETECTOR` in the mask and produce an unlabelled CSV. The warning catches that user error too.

Want me to commit the bundle (cv_marvin_v1 fix + recording prepend + export-ml warning + first-row-zero timestamp + journal entries)?

```bash
marvin-perf: SensiML CSV export for MPLAB ML training data

End-to-end pipeline from a marvin-perf capture to a labelled CSV ready
for import into MPLAB Machine Learning Development Suite / SensiML
Data Capture Lab. v0 produces five independent binary classifiers
(one per fret), label = cv_marvin_v1 pressed_mask, sensors = fretboard
phototransistors at the upstream sense line.

Tool (tools/marvin-perf):
- New `marvin-perf export-ml <capture> --out <csv>` subcommand. Streams
  the capture, walks records once with a latest-detector cursor, emits
  one row per FRETBOARD_RAW with timestamp + 5 ADC + 5 binary labels.
  Schema matches the MPLAB Data Visualizer "SensiML CSV" preset; first
  row's timestamp is 0.0 to match the "elapsed since logging started"
  convention.
- Loud non-zero exit + warning when the export emits no detector records
  or no rows — surfaces the easy-to-miss "I forgot to enable a type"
  failure mode that previously produced a structurally-valid but
  training-useless CSV.
- 8 new tests in test_export_sensiml_csv.py cover schema, row count,
  ADC passthrough, label step-function, timestamp arithmetic, strict
  vs non-strict pre-detector handling, and the missing-SESSION error.

Web recorder (tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py):
- Cache the framed bytes of the most-recent SESSION and DETECTOR_CONFIG
  records in `_State.prepend_framed`. On record_start, prepend them to
  the new bin so it's self-contained from byte 0 even when recording
  starts mid-session — without this, every web-mode recording missed
  SESSION (one-shot per sink-attach) and the exporter couldn't recover
  timer_freq_hz.

Firmware (firmware/marvin):
- Wire PerfLog_EmitDetector into cv_marvin_v1's detect_frame. The
  function had been defined and declared but never called: cv was
  building detector_state_t and posting it to the actuator bus
  (game played correctly) without mirroring to perf-log. This is why
  the first hardware export run produced 0 DETECTOR records despite
  bit 3 being set in the firmware mask.

Journal entries cover all three fixes; verification described in
docs/journal.md session-log.
EOF
```
